title: Inner/outer html of element
description: Get the inner or outer html of a htmlelement as a htmldocument.

title: Tag name of element
description: Get the tag name of an element.

title: Title of document
description: Get the html title of a document.

title: Load Chunk
description: Loads or unloads the specified chunk.

title: URL Safe Text
description: Converts a text into a text safe for usage in URLs. This can be useful for injecting user input into a URL (e.g. when using a search api).

title: Dimension
description: A Minecraft world's dimension, also known as an environment.
type_usage: end the_end nether normal

title: Server Socket Is Open
description: Checks whether there is a server socket open at the specified host and port. Optionally, you can specify a timeout for how long to try checking before giving up.
syntax_pattern: server socket is open at host %string% port %number% [with timeout of %-timespan%]

title: Server List Ping
description: Called when a Minecraft client pings the server to show information in the server list.

title: Tab Complete
description: Called when a player uses tab to auto complete a message or a command. Only available in recent Bukkit versions. Also see the Completions and Last Token expressions.

title: JSON Safe Text
description: Converts a text into a text safe for usage in JSON strings. This can be useful for injecting user input into a JSON payload (e.g. when using a search api).

title: Border Stabilize
description: Called when a border (optionally only of the specified world(s)) stops moving.

title: Chunk is Loaded
description: Checks whether the specified chunk is loaded.

title: FunctionSocket Is Open
description: Checks whether there is a function socket open at the specified port.
syntax_pattern: function socket is open at port %number%

title: Vectors - Vector from Location
description: Creates a vector from a location.

title: Hang
description: Called when an entity is hung. Can be cancelled. Also see the Hanged Entity expression.

title: Unhang
description: Called when an entity is unhung. Can be cancelled. Optionally, you can specify hanging remove causes which make the trigger only be called if the unhanging is due to those reasons. Also see the Hanged Entity expression.

title: Packet Event
description: Called when a packet of one of the specified types is being sent or received.

title: Login Result
description: An expression, for use in the 'on connect' event, for the result of the connection attempt. See the PlayerLoginResult type for possible values.

title: Loaded Scripts
description: An expression for the names of all of the currently loaded scripts.

title: Last Token
description: An expression, used in the Tab Complete and Chat Tab Complete events, for the last token typed by the player before tab completing.

title: Chunk is Slimey
description: Checks whether the specified chunk is slimey.

title: Note Play
description: Called when a noteblock is played.

title: Armor Stand Place
description: Called when an armor stand is placed

title: Chat Tab Complete
description: Called when a player uses tab to auto complete a message (not a command). Also see the Completions and Last Token expressions.

title: Last Called Custom Event was Cancelled
description: Checks whether the last custom event that was called in this trigger was or wasn't cancelled. This expression/condition is unaffected by whether another section of code calls a custom event. See the Call Custom Event effect for more info about custom events.

title: Living Entity is Collidable
description: Checks whether the specified living entity is collidable. Note that it is possible that an entity is non-collidable due to circumstance (ex. the entity is dead) and this condition/expression still be true as the entity would normally be collidable. In addition, if an entity that is collidable collides with another entity that is non-collidable due to this condition/expression being false, they will still collide.

title: On GriefPrevention - Save Trapped Player
description: Called when a trapped player is saved.

title: Unix Date
description: Converts given Unix timestamp to a date. The Unix timespan represents the number of seconds elapsed since 1 January 1970.

title: Fill Region in ChunkData
description: Fills a region in the specified chunkdata with the specified material:1. Fills a region between two coordinates in the specified chunkdata2. Fills the specified layer of the specified chunkdata3. Fills the layers from the first to the second specified layer in the specified chunkdata
syntax_pattern:
fill region from %number%, %number%, %number% to %number%, %number%, %number% in %chunkdata% with %itemstack%
fill layer %number% in %chunkdata% with %itemstack%
fill layers %number% to %number% in %chunkdata% with %itemstack%

title: Add Elements to List
description: A ListUtil effect (see the ListUtil expression for more info). Adds the specified elements before or after the specified index or the end of the specified list.

title: Map JSON to Variable
description:
Copies JSON formatted text into a list variable. Existing entries in the list variable are not deleted.

If the following JSON were mapped to variable `{json::*}`
```json
{
  "foo": 15,
  "bar": "test",
  "baz": {
    "foobar": [
      {
        "quux": false
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
the following assertions would be true:
```
{json::foo} is 15
{json::bar} is "test"
{json::baz} is true                    # special case
{json::baz::foobar} is true            # special case
{json::baz::foobar::1} is true         # special case
{json::baz::foobar::1::quux} is false
```
The variables marked `# special case` contain nested JSON objects and are true so Skript can properly loop through the variable. These variables (like `{json::baz}`, not list variables like `{json::baz::*}`) can be deleted and the structure will still properly serialize into JSON.

title: Move Elements of List
description: Uses either the Element of List or Some Elements of List expression (both are ListUtil expressions) as the first specified expression, and moves them forward or backward the specified amount in their specified list.

title: Request is Accepted
description: Used in the 'on handshake' section of a websocket server template. Checks whether the client's request was accepted or refused. Can be set.

title: Border is Moving
description: Checks whether the border of the specified world is moving or stable (not moving).

title: Async Set
description: Evaluates the second specified expression asynchronously, then sets the specified variable (the first specified expression) to that value and continues the rest of the code synchronously.

title: Structure Settings of Creator
description: An condition/expression for whether a creator is set to generate structures.
syntax_pattern:
[the] struct of %creator%
%creator%'[s] struct
[the] structures of %creator%
%creator%'[s] structures
[the] structure settings of %creator%
%creator%'[s] structure settings

title: Is Beyond Border
description: Checks whether a location/entity is beyond or within the border in its world.

title: Async Wait
description: The asynchronous equivalent of Skript's built-in 'wait %timespan%' effect, as just using that effect in asynchronous code will make the rest of the code run synchronously.

title: Play Note on Noteblock
description: Plays the specified noteblock, optionally with a specified instrument and a specified note.

title: Members
description:
Returns a list of the fields, methods, or constructors of an object, including their modifiers and parameters.

If you need a list of field or method names without modifier or parameter details, see [Member Names](https://skripthub.net/docs/?id=2928) expression.

title: Living Entity
description: A living entity, i.e. a mob or player, not inanimate entities like projectiles or dropped items.
type_usage: see entity, but ignore inanimate objects

title: Scores are Enabled
description: Checks whether the tablist(s) of the specified player(s) have scores enabled. This only applies to enabling scores using MundoSK's tablist syntaxes.
syntax_pattern:
scores [are] (enabled|disabled) in tablist of %players%
scores [are] (enabled|disabled) in %players%'s tablist

title: PlotSquared | Plot Home
description: Get/Set the home of a plot

title: Send Packet
description: Sends the specified packet(s) to the specified player(s).

title: Open Function Socket
description: Opens a function socket at the port specified. A function socket receives messages and executes a function, messaging back the function's return value if it has one. The port has to be a port that isn't already in use (Ex. Don't use your Minecraft server's port). The password is an optional string used for security, and the function is the handler function that will handle the messages received through the function socket
syntax_pattern: open function socket at port %number% [with password %-string%] [through function %-string%]

title: Write to Socket
description: Sends a message through a socket. The host can either be the address or the IP. The timeout part is how many seconds to wait before stopping a socket write function if it doesn't make a connection or error out. The last part is if you want to handle a response through a handler function.
syntax_pattern: write %strings% to socket with host %string% port %number% [with timeout %-timespan%] [to handle response through function %-string% with id %-string%]

title: Clear Player Tab Modifications
description: Resets all of the tabs representing players for the specified player(s) to normal. This will make all players visible in the tablist and reset any display name, latency, and score changes.

title: Delete All Simple Tabs
description: Removes all simple tabs from the tablist(s) of the specified players(s).

title: Show or Hide in Tablist
description: Shows or hides certain players for other certain players in their tablist(s). Note: if the Players Are Visible condition/expression is set to false for a specific player and you show a player for them using this effect, then the condition/expression will become true but only that player will become unhidden.
syntax_pattern:
(show|hide) [player] tab[s] of %players% for %players%
(show|hide) %players%'s [player] tab[s] for %players%
(show|hide) %players% for %players% in tablist
(show|hide) %players% in %players%'s tablist
(show|hide) %players% in [the] tablist of %players%

title: Print Stack Trace
description: Prints the stack trace of the specified throwable (error/exception).

title: Stop WebSocket Server
description: Stops the WebSocket server at the specified port, optionally specifying a timeout in milliseconds.
syntax_pattern: stop websocket server at port %number% [with timeout %-number%]

title: WebSocket Send
description: Sends the specified messages through the specified websockets. If no websockets are specified, the messages are sent through the event-websocket.

title: Latency of Player Tab
description: An expression for the amount of latency bars of the specified player tab in the tablist of the specified player(s). When set, this is always between 0 and 5. This will not be set if the player tab is hidden.
syntax_pattern:
(latency|ping) of [player] tab of %player% for %players%
(latency|ping) of %player%'s [player] tab for %players%
tablist (latency|ping) of %player% for %players%
%player%'s tablist (latency|ping) for %players%

title: New WebSocket
description: Creates a new websocket connection using the websocket client with the specified id, connecting to the specified URI.Optionally, you can specify additional HTTP headers, which you can use to add additional information in the initial connection (ex. a password). A header is a mapping from one string (the name) to another (the value). Each header has a unique name.You can specify headers by creating a new handshake, setting its headers, and then specifying it in the syntax here. Keep in mind that any other information stored in the handshake will be ignored by this expression.

title: Create Simple Tab
description: Creates a simple tab for the specified player(s) with the specified id and properties. If a specified player already has a simple tab with the specified id in their tablist, that tab will not be modified and no new tab will be created. This effect will not work for a specified player if they have the array tablist enabled.
syntax_pattern: create ([simple] tab [with] id|simple tab) %string% for %players% with [display] name %string% [(ping|latency) %-number%] [(head|icon|skull) %-skin%] [score %-number%]

title: Delete Simple Tab
description: Removes the simple tab with the specified id from the tablist(s) of the specified player(s).

title: Close WebSocket
description: Closes the specified websocket connection, optionally specifying a closing message to send.

title: Start WebSocket Server
description: Starts a WebSocket server using the specified server template at the specified port. A WebSocket server allows other servers/online services to initiate websocket connections with the server.

title: PlotSquared | Average Rating
description: Get the average rating of a plot

title: Receive Packet
description: Makes the server simulate receiving the specified packet(s) from the specified player(s)

title: Close Function Socket
description: Closes the function socket at the port specified. See the Open Function Socket Effect for more info.

title: Song from Id
description: The song from the registry using its id.

title: Load World Automatically
description: Tells MundoSK whether it should load the specified world automatically on server start. This is useful for simple and straightforward world management without the need for a world management plugin. Don't run this effect with the main world, as Bukkit will already load that world automatically, and this effect can't be used to enable/disable that behavior.

title: Romanize/Transliterate
description: Transliterates the given Cyrillic text into english.

title: Unload World
description: Unloads the specified world. You can specify whether or not to save before unloading (this defaults to true).

title: Case
description:
Not an effect, but rather a scope (written with a colon at the end with a section of indented code under it, like an if statement or loop). 
The case scope is written underneath a switch scope, specifying an object which, if equal to the switch scope's specified object, will cause the case scope's underlying code block to be run.

title: Switch
description:
Not an effect, but rather a scope (written with a colon at the end with a section of indented code under it, like an if statement or loop). 
The switch scope allows you to specify an object, then below the switch scope, insert case scopes, and when run, the switch scope will go through each case scope and check which one is equal to the switch scope's object, then run that case scope's code block.

title: Sync in Timespan
description:
Not an effect, but rather a scope (written with a colon at the end with a section of indented code under it, like an if statement or loop). 
A scope used to run a certain block of code synchronously. This means that the code will be run on the main server thread, allowing you to perform tasks relating to Bukkit, such as changing a block. This is useful when code running asynchronously needs to perform such tasks. Optionally, you can specify a timespan to wait before running the block of code. The lines of code following the scope will run as normal without waiting for any of the block of code to start/finish. It is also possible to write this scope as a regular line of code, in which case instead of a block of code below a scope, all following lines of code will be forced to run synchronously, as well as wait a certain timespan if it is specified (this behavior is mostly equivalent to Skript's 'wait %timespan%' effect).

title: Create World
description: Creates a world with the specified name, optionally with a few settings. See the environment type and worldtype type for valid environments and worldtypes respectively. Generator settings can either be custom superflat codes or customized world codes (for customized world codes the worldtype needs to be 'customized').

title: Delete World
description: Deletes the specified world. The specified world must be loaded in order to be deleted.

title: PlotSquared | Plot Biome
description: Get the biome of a plot

title: Reset World Border
description: Resets the border properties of the specified world to their default values. These values can be found at https://minecraft.gamepedia.com/World_border#Commands

title: Create World using Creator
description: Creates a world using the specified creator, optionally specifying the world's name (this is required if the creator doesn't specify a name).See the creator expressions for more information on how to specify the world's name and other settings. If a world with the name (specified or from the creator) already exists, this will just load that world instead of creating a new one.

title: Duplicate World
description: Creates a copy of the specified world using the specified string as a name. The specified world must be loaded in order for this to work.

title: Invited Players
description: The invited players of a faction

title: Last Activity of Faction Player
description: Gets the last activity of a faction player

title: Leader of Faction
description: The leader of a faction

title: Factions Plugin Name
description: The currently used faction plugin's name

title: Id of Faction
description: The id of a faction

title: Try
description:
Not an effect, but rather a scope (written with a colon at the end with a section of indented code under it, like an if statement or loop). 
A scope used for running code that may throw a throwable (error/exception). If a throwable is thrown, the rest of the code under try is not run. If there is a 'catch in %object%' scope following the 'try' scope, the code under the catch scope is run with the thrown throwable being stored in the specified variable. The rest of the code outside of the try and catch scopes proceeds as normal afterwards.

title: Code Block
description: A block of code that can be run to perform certain effects.

title: Chunk Data
description: Represents a 3-dimensional grid of itemstacks. Used in world generators to manipulate the blocks in the chunk to be generated.

title: HangingRemoveCause
description: A cause for a hanged entity to have been unhung.
type_usage: default physics obstruction explosion entity

title: Throwable
description: An exception or error.

title: Block - is Full Block
description:
Checks if a block is a full block (like dirt, stone, endstone).
Essentially checks if a block is 1x1x1 and only has one mesh.
syntax_pattern:
%blocks/blockstates% (is|are) [a] full block[s]
%blocks/blockstates% (isn't|is not|aren't|are not) [a] full block[s]

title: Random Chance
description:
Not an effect, but rather a scope (written with a colon at the end with a section of indented code under it, like an if statement or loop). 
The probability scope is used to perform different actions based on given probabilities. Under the scope, you write different probability values using the syntax '%number% prob[ability]'. These can be written as scopes or just simple lines of code. When the probability scope is run, all of these probabilities are added up and then, using their values, one is chosen at random and the code starts to proceed from there. First, if the chosen probability is a scope, its section of code is run. Then, the rest of the lines of code after the chosen probability are run. If another probability is encountered, it is ignored and the section of code under it (if it is a scope) is also ignored, but the lines of code that come after it are still run.

title: Catch
description:
Not an effect, but rather a scope (written with a colon at the end with a section of indented code under it, like an if statement or loop). 
A scope that is used following a 'try' scope to process a throwable (error/exception) if it is thrown. The thrown throwable is stored in the specified variable and then the code under the scope is run.

title: Biome Grid
description: Represents a 2-dimensional grid of biomes. Used in world generators to manipulate the biome(s) in the chunk to be generated.

title: Difficulty
description: The difficulty of a world.
type_usage: hard normal easy peaceful

title: Instrument
description: An instrument to which a note can be played using a noteblock.
type_usage: xylophone chime guitar bell flute bass_guitar sticks snare_drum bass_drum piano

title: JSONObject
description: A JSONObject, a type of data structure used for storing information in the form of keys/indexes and values (like a list variable). Useful in Skript for transmitting complex information that isn't represented by a type in cases where list variables can't be used (ex. returning values from expressions/functions (ex. the JSON Field of Packet expression)).

title: Random
description: An object that can be used to generate random or pseudo-random numbers.

title: Packet
description: A packet. Packets are used by the Minecraft client and server to transmit information, and can be intercepted, read, and modified in order to gain information and modify the behavior of your server in certain ways that are not possible through Bukkit.

title: Skin Texture
description: Represents a skin, possibly of a player. Write 'steve' or 'alex' for these respective skins.

title: Stack Trace Element
description: An element (line) of a stack trace. The stack trace is the huge blob of text you get in your console when an uncaught exception occurs on your server.

title: Handshake
description: A handshake, sent by two websockets to each other when they are initially connection. Handshakes contain information necessary to initiate a websocket connection and you can add more information (ex. a password) that you want to be sent on the initial connection.

title: Packet Info Alias
description: Not an actual event, but rather a group of packet info aliases to be used with packets of the specified packettype. Packet info aliases are aliases for specific usages of packet info expressions. Under the main scope lines are written in the form '<new syntax> = <old syntax>', where the old syntax is how you would normally write an expression for the desired packet info, and the new syntax is how you want to be able to write it. Note that the new syntax is essentially being registered as a Skript syntax, so you can write it with features of Skript syntax like optional parts enclosed in '[]', and multiple usages of '%packet%' are allowed in your syntax, though only one of them should be possible to use at a time since only one packet is used to evaluate the alias (and your syntax must always require an instance of '%packet%' to be used). A small addition to normal Skript syntax is that now, if you would like to have a group of different options for syntax but also have the whole thing be optional, instead of writing '[(a|b|...)]' you can write '[a|b|...]'.

title: Title of Book
description: An expression for the title of the specified book.

title: Block in Chunk
description: The first is the block at the specified coordinates within the specified chunk The second is a center or corner block of a layer, one of the three defaults or a specified number, of the specified chunk.

title: ID of Custom Event
description: An expression, used in the Custom Event event, for either the primary id, or all ids (MundoSK 1.8+), of the custom event that was called. The primary id means the one that was listed first when calling the custom event. See the Call Custom Event effect for more info.

title: Enchanted Book with Enchantments
description: An expression for an enchanted book identical to the one specified but also carrying the specified enchantments.

title: Player Tab is Visible
description: Checks whether the first player's tab is visible for the second specified player(s).
syntax_pattern:
[player] tab of %player% is (visible|hidden) for %players%
%player%'s [player] tab is (visible|hidden) for %players%
%player% is (visible|hidden) in %players%'s tablist
%player% is (visible|hidden) in tablist (of|for) %players%

title: Author of Book
description: An expression for the author of the specified book.

title: New Book
description: An expression for a book with the specified title, author, and pages.

title: Blocks in Chunk
description:
The first is all of the blocks in the specified chunk.
The second is the blocks between two coordinates of the specified chunk.
The third is a layer, one of the three defaults or a specified number, of the specified chunk.
The fourth is the layers between two specified numbers of the specified chunk.
syntax_pattern:
[all] blocks (of|in) %chunk%
blocks [from] %number%, %number%, %number% to %number%, %number%, %number% (of|in) %chunk%
(layer %-number%|top|bottom|sea level) (of|in) %chunk%
[[blocks] from] (layer %-number%|top|bottom|sea level) to (layer %-number%|top|bottom|sea level) (of|in) %chunk%
layers [from] %number% to %number% (of|in) %chunk%

title: Chunk at Coordinates
description:
The first is the chunk at the specified coordinates.
The second is the chunks between the specified coordinates.
The third is the chunk that contains the specified location.
The fourth is the chunks between the specified locations.
syntax_pattern:
chunk %number%, %number% [in %world%]
chunks [from] %number%, %number% to %number%, %number% [in %world%]
chunk at %location%
chunks from %location% to %location%

title: Coordinate of Chunk
description: The x or z-coordinate of the specified chunk

title: World of Chunk
description: The world in which the specified chunk is located

title: World Creator
description: A creator is a way to store data about the various properties of a world for creating it, and can be used in the Create World effect and in Automatic Creator syntax elements to load worlds automatically. See the Property of Creator expressions for more information.

title: WorldType
description: A Minecraft world's world type.
type_usage: version 1.1 large biomes superflat customized amplified large_biomes version_1_1 flat normal

title: Page ListUtil
description: A ListUtil specifier (see the ListUtil expression for more info) that allows you to manipulate the pages of a book. This is done by, in a ListUtil effect or expression, writing 'page' where '%listutil%' is, and inputting a book for '%objects%'.

title: Code Block of Function
description: An expression for the codeblock form of the specified function.

title: Args of Custom Event
description: An expression, used in the Custom Event event, for a list of the arguments, if any, that were specified for this particular custom event call. See the Call Custom Event effect for more info.
syntax_pattern:
args of custom event
custom event's args

title: Normal/Maximum/Boosting Power
description: The normal/maximum/boosting power of a faction or player

title: Open State of Faction
description: Gets whether a faction is open or not

title: Peaceful State of Faction
description: Gets whether a faction is peaceful or not

title: Relation Change (Wish) Sender/Target Faction
description: Gets the sender/target faction of a relation change (wish)

title: Members of Faction
description: The members of a faction

title: Name of Faction
description: The name of a faction

title: Amount of Elements in List
description: A ListUtil expression (see the ListUtil expression for more info) for the size of the specified list.

title: Enable or Disable Array Tablist
description: Enables or disables array tablist in the specified or all tablist(s) The array tablist creates a grid of tabs that allows you to use grid coordinates to easily modify individual tabs. When enabling, you can specify the amount of columns (defaults to 4), the amount of rows (defaults to 20), and the initial icon (defaults to a white texture). See the Size of Array Tablist and Icon of Array Tab expressions for more info. Note that it is recommended to use the default tablist dimensions of 4x20 to avoid issues with skins. If the array tablist is already enabled, it will be replaced with a blank one matching the new specifications. Note that when enabling the array tablist, all simple tabs will be removed and all player tabs will be hidden. When disabling the array tablist, all player tabs will be visible, and there will be no simple tabs.
syntax_pattern:
(enable|activate) [the] array tablist [for (%-players%|group %-string%)] [with [%-number% columns] [%-number% rows] [(default|initial) (head|icon|player_head) %-skin%]]
(disable|deactivate) [the] array tablist [for (%-players%|group %-string%)]

title: Element of List
description: A ListUtil expression (see the ListUtil expression for more info) for the element at the specified index or the last element in the specified list.

title: All Types
description: An expression for a list of all of the registered types.

title: Branch
description: An expression, used in a tree loop, for the full index, or branch, of the current value in the tree loop's list variable.

title: Breath of Living Entity
description: An expression for the amount of breath (the bubbles that appear on the hotbar when you go underwater)  of the specified underwater living entity, or its maximum possible breath.
syntax_pattern:
[the] breath of %livingentity%
%livingentity%'[s] breath
[the] max breath of %livingentity%
%livingentity%'[s] max breath

title: Destination
description: An expression, used in the 'on teleport' event, for the destination of the teleporting entity.

title: Difficulty of World
description: An expression for the difficulty of the specified world. See the Difficulty type for values.

title: Elements that Are
description: An expression for a list of the elements in the specified list that are either equal or not equal to the latter specified object.

title: Hanged Entity
description: An expression, used in the Hang and Unhang events, for the entity which was hung/unhung.

title: Highest Solid Block
description: An expression for the highest block that isn't air at a specific location. Useful for setting spawns.

title: Indexes of List Variable
description: An expression for all of the indexes used in the specified list variable. This includes indexes that refer to sub-variables, ex. if {_ex::pie::temp} is set, then "pie" will be included if {_ex::*} is specified as in this expression.

title: IP of Pinger
description: An expression, used in the Server List Ping event, for the IP of the pinging client.

title: IP of Server
description: An expression for the IP of your Minecraft server.

title: JSON from List Variable
description: An expression for a jsonobject constructed from the information stored inside the specified list variable.

title: Block - is Waterlogged
description: Checks whether or not one or more blocks, blockstates or blockdatas are waterlogged.

title: Biome in Biome Grid
description: An expression for the biome at the specified x and z coordinates the specified biomegrid.

title: Some Elements of List
description: A ListUtil expression (see the ListUtil expression for more info) for the sublist of the specified list from the first specified index to the second specified index or the end of the list.

title: Completions
description: An editable expression, used in the Tab Complete and Chat Tab Complete events, for a list of all completions available for this tab complete.

title: For Elements
description: An expression that, for each element of the last specified list, stores that element in the specified variable ('%object%'), and calculates a value (or multiple) by evaluating the first specified expression, then returns all of the calculated values. For example, evaluating '({_x} + 1) for {_x} in 1, 2, 3' would return '2, 3, 4'.

title: Current Chunk Coordinates
description: An expression, used in the 'generation' section of a custom generator, for a coordinate of the chunk currently being generated

title: Material in Chunk Data
description: An expression for the material the specified coordinates in the specified chunkdata.

title: All Elements of List
description: A ListUtil expression (see the ListUtil expression for more info) for all of the elements in the specified list.

title: Return Type of Function
description: An expression for the return type of the function with the specified name.

title: Shown Amount of Players
description: An expression, used in the Server List Ping event, for the amount of players currently online or max amount of players allowed that was shown by your server to the pinging client.

title: Random Value from Random
description: A random value of the specified type, either from a specified random, or from an arbitrary one. In the case of the 'int less than' syntax, the random value will be an int greater than or equal to 0 but less than the specified number.

title: Shown MOTD
description: An expression, used in the Server List Ping event, for the MOTD shown by your server to the pinging client.

title: Color Blueprint
description: Colors all of the specified blueprint as the specified color. Normally the blueprint you specify will be a section of a larger blueprint, as we normally don't need skins that are a single color.

title: On Citizen Create
description: Called when a citizen is created.

title: Number as Java Type
description:
An expression for getting the specified number as the specified Java primitive type:
b = byte
d = double
f = float
s = short
l = long
This is useful for example when modifying certain fields of packets, as they frequently require certain Java number types and will cause errors when the wrong type is used.

title: Note of Noteblock
description: The current note of the specified noteblock.

title: Port of Server
description: An expression for the port of your Minecraft server.

title: Respawn Location
description: An expression, used in the 'on respawn' event, for the location at which a player respawned.

title: New Nether Portal
description: An expression, used in the 'on [player] portal' event, that attempts to create a new nether portal within the specified radius of the specified location, and returns the location of the created portal if successful, and is not set otherwise.
syntax_pattern: new nether portal within [[a] radius of] %number% (block|meter)s of %location%

title: Tree at Location
description: An expression for the blocks that make up a tree which has a block at the specified location. Note that if two trees are connected through leaves or wood, both of their blocks (and the blocks of any further connected trees) will be returned.

title: Value of Gamerule
description: An expression for the value of the specified gamerule in the specified world.

title: World from Name
description: An expression for the world with the specified name.

title: Entity Field of Packet
description: An expression for an entity field of a packet (first see the Packet Info expression for a more general explanation of packet fields). The specified world is used to determine which world to get the entity from, and thus should be specified as whichever world the player sending/receiving the packet is in.

title: Enum Field of Packet
description: An expression for an enum field of a packet (first see the Packet Info o expression for a more general explanation of packet fields). The specified string is the name of the enum you are getting/setting. Using arbitrary gives you access to all enum fields, rather than just one particular type, and allows you to access certain enums that are NMS types rather than ProtocolLib and thus can't be accessed by their name.

title: HTTP Header of Handshake
description: An expression for the value of the HTTP header with the specified name of the specified handshake.

title: On Citizen Despawn
description: Called when a citizen is despawned.

title: On Citizen Spawn
description: Called when a citizen is spawned.

title: Citizen Is Navigating
description: Checks if a citizen is navigating.

title: Citizen Is Paused
description: Checks if a citizen is paused.

title: Entity Is Citizen
description: Checks if an entity is a citizen.

title: Cancel Citizen Navigation
description: Cancels/Stops the navigation of a citizen.

title: New Random
description: An expression for a new random from the specified seed, or an arbitrary seed.

title: Animate Citizen
description:
Makes a citizen do the given animation.

arm swing, arm swing offhand, crit, eat food, hurt, magic crit, sit, sleep, sneak, start elytra, start use mainhand item, start use offhand item, stop sitting, stop sleeping, stop sneaking and stop use item

title: New Packet
description: An expression for a new packet of the specified type.

title: Random Index from List Variable
description: An expression that takes a list variable containing numbers, then adds all of the numbers up, assigns each index a probability based on its number value divided by the total sum, and finally chooses one index at random using the probabilities and returns it.

title: On ShopChest - Shop Removal
description: Called when a shop is removed.

title: On ShopChest - Transaction
description: Called when a player buys/sells something from a shop.

title: Nametag of Player
description: An expression for the nametag (the name that appears above a player's head) of the specified player. If target ('for') players are specified, the expression will return a nametag for each target player specified.

title: Retrieved Skin
description:
An expression for a skin retrieved using the Mineskin API:
A skin recreated from the specified image file,
A skin recreated from the specified URL of an image, or
The skin of the specified offline player retrieved from Mojang

title: Skull from Skin
description: An expression for a skull bearing the specified skin, optionally with the specified owner. If you do not specify an owner, the owner will appear to be "MundoSK-Name". This really only matters if anybody is going to actually have the skull in their inventory (i.e. if the skull is only going to be used as a block, the owner isn't important, though it may be useful as an identifier).

title: Handler of Function Socket
description: An expression for the handler function of the function socket.
syntax_pattern: handler [function] of function socket at port %number%

title: Skin with Value
description: An expression for a skin with the specified value and signature.

title: Player Count of Server
description: An expression for the player count or maximum allowed player count of the server at the specified host and port. Make sure to get this expression asynchronously (under 'async', for example), as otherwise your server may lag.
syntax_pattern: (player count|max player count) of server with host %string% [port %-number%]

title: Display Name of Array Tab
description: An expression for the display name of the specified array tab for the specified player(s).

title: Password of Function Socket
description: An expression for the password of the function socket at that port. **For clarification, this only gets the password from function sockets on your server, not other servers.
syntax_pattern: pass[word] of function socket at port %number%

title: Display Name of Simple Tab
description: An expression for the display name of the simple tab with the specified id in the tablist(s) of the specified player(s).
syntax_pattern: [display] name of ([simple] tab [with] id|simple tab) %string% for %players%

title: Random Index from Numbers
description: An expression that takes a list of numbers, then adds all of the numbers up, assigns each index (here, index means the position of a number in the list, ex. the first number has an index of 1) a probability based on its number value divided by the total sum, and finally chooses one index at random using the probabilities and returns it.

title: All Groups
description:
This will return a list of all the groups currently registered by PermissionsEx.

Can be used with: 
Delete - deletes all groups registered by PermissionsEx, I personally wouldn't suggest using this

title: Citizen Attack/Follow
description: Makes a citizen attack or follow an entity.

title: Number Array Field of Packet
description: An expression for int array and byte array fields of packets. First see the Packet Info expression for a more general explanation of packet fields.

title: Type of Packet
description: An expression for the packettype of the specified packet.

title: Number Field of Packet
description: An expression for different kinds of number fields of packets. First see the Packet Info expression for a more general explanation of packet fields.

title: MOTD of Server
description: An expression foro the MOTD of the server at the specified host and port. Make sure to get this expression asynchronously (under 'async', for example), as otherwise your server may lag.

title: Create Citizen
description: Creates a citizen with name, type and optional location.

title: Despawn Citizen
description: Despawns a spawned citizen.

title: Destroy Citizen
description: Destroys a citizen.

title: Score of Array Tab
description: An expression for the score of the specified array tab for the specified player(s).

title: ShopChest - All Shops of Player
description: Returns the IDs of all shops of a  Player.
syntax_pattern:
[(all [[of] the]|the)] [IDs of all [the]] [ShopChest] shops of %offlineplayer%
[all of] [[the] IDs of [all]] %offlineplayer%'s [ShopChest] shops

title: Score of Player Tab
description: An expression for the score of the specified player tab in the tablist of the specified player(s). This will not be set if the player tab is hidden.
syntax_pattern:
score of [player] tab of %player% for %players%
score of %player%'s [player] tab for %players%
tablist score of %player% for %players%
%player%'s tablist score for %players%

title: ShopChest - Shop At Location
description: Returns the id of the shop at a location.

title: Cause of Throwable
description: An expression for the cause, if any, of the specified throwable (error/exception).

title: Details of Throwable
description: An expression for the details of the specified throwable (error/exception).

title: Line Number of Stack Trace Element
description: An expression for the line number of the line of code described by the specified stacktraceelement.

title: Property Name of Stack Trace Element
description: An expression for the name of the specified stacktraceelement's class, file, or method.
syntax_pattern:
[the] class name of %stacktraceelement%
%stacktraceelement%'[s] class name
[the] file name of %stacktraceelement%
%stacktraceelement%'[s] file name
[the] method name of %stacktraceelement%
%stacktraceelement%'[s] method name

title: Stack Trace of Throwable
description: An expression for the stack trace (as a list of stack trace elements) of the specified throwable (error/exception). The stack trace is the huge blob of text you get in your console when an uncaught exception occurs on your server.

title: All WebSockets of Server
description: An expression for all of the websocket connections of the websocket server at the specified port. When used under 'websocket server %string%', the port is optional, in which case it will return the websockets for the websocket server being controlled.

title: Content of Handshake
description: An expression for the content (a byte array) stored in the specified handshake.

title: HTTP Header Names of Handshake
description: An expression for a list of the names of the HTTP headers of the specified handshake.

title: Connection State of WebSocket
description: An expression for the connection state of the specified websocket.

title: Host of WebSocket
description: An expression for the host, local or external, of the specified websocket.
syntax_pattern:
[the] local host of %websocket%
%websocket%'[s] local host
[the] remote host of %websocket%
%websocket%'[s] remote host
[the] external host of %websocket%
%websocket%'[s] external host

title: Move Citizen
description: Makes a citizen move to a specific location with optional speed.

title: Pause/Continue Citizen Navigation
description: Pauses/Continues the navigation of a citizen.

title: Latency of Array Tab
description: An expression for the amount of latency bars of the specified array tab for the specified player(s). This is always between 0 and 5.

title: Latency of Simple Tab
description: An expression for the amount of latency bars of the simple tab with the specified id in the tablist(s) of the specified player(s). This is always between 0 and 5.

title: Score of Simple Tab
description: An expression for the score of the simple tab with the specified id in the tablist(s) of the specified player(s).
syntax_pattern: score of ([simple] tab [with] id|simple tab) %string% for %players%

title: Tablist Header or Footer
description: An expression for the header or footer of the tablist(s) of the specified player(s). This is a list expression as the header and footer can have multiple lines of text.

title: Spawn Citizen
description: Spawns a citizen at specific location.

title: All Citizens
description: Returns all citizens.

title: Citizen ID
description: Returns the ID of a citizen. Cannot be changed.

title: ShopChest - Shop Buy Price
description: Returns the buy price of a shop.

title: ShopChest - Shop Limit
description: Returns the shop limit of a player.

title: Property of Border
description:
An expression for a certain property of the specified world's border:
diameter: The diameter/size/side length (Note: you should use 'diameter' instead of 'size' to refer to this property, as 'size' conflicts with Skript's size expression)
damage amount: The amount of damage a player will take per second if they are outside both the border and the damage buffer
damage buffer: The distance (in blocks) outside of the border a player can be before taking damage
warning distance: The distance a player has to be within the border to see the red warning effect
warning time: The amount of time the border should be within of reaching a player to show that player the red warning effect.
syntax_pattern:
((diameter|side length|size)|damage amount|damage buffer|warning distance|warning time) of %world%
%world%'s ((diameter|side length|size)|damage amount|damage buffer|warning distance|warning time)

title: Server Icon
description: A server icon that was loaded using the load server icon effect.

title: Time Remaining Until Border Stabilize
description: An expression for the timespan remaining until the border of the specified world stops moving.
syntax_pattern:
(time remaining|remaining time) until [the] border stabilize[s] (of|in) %world%
%world%'s (time remaining|remaining time) until [the] border stabilize[s]

title: Creator of World
description: An expression for a creator with the properties of the specified world.

title: Dimension of Creator
description: An expression for the dimension, or environment, of a creator. This is 'normal' by default.
syntax_pattern:
[the] dim of %creator%
%creator%'[s] dim
[the] dimension of %creator%
%creator%'[s] dimension
[the] env of %creator%
%creator%'[s] env
[the] environment of %creator%
%creator%'[s] environment

title: Generator of Creator
description: An expression for the custom generator of a creator. This will not be set if a creator is not specified to use a custom generator.
syntax_pattern:
[the] gen of %creator%
%creator%'[s] gen
[the] generator of %creator%
%creator%'[s] generator

title: Generator Settings of Creator
description: An expression for the generator settings of a creator. This can be a superflat world code or customized world code (the worldtype must be set as superflat and customized respectively in these cases). In addition, a custom generator might also use generator settings.
syntax_pattern:
[the] gen set of %creator%
%creator%'[s] gen set
[the] generator set of %creator%
%creator%'[s] generator set
[the] gen settings of %creator%
%creator%'[s] gen settings
[the] generator settings of %creator%
%creator%'[s] generator settings

title: Teleport Cause
description: The teleport cause in a teleport event.

title: Spawn Reason
description: The spawn reason in a spawn event.

title: ID of WebSocket Client
description: An expression for the ID of the websocket client template controlling the specified websocket. This will not be set if the specified websocket belongs to a websocket server (meaning the connection was initiated externally).

title: ID of WebSocket Server
description: An expression for the ID of the websocket server template controlling the websocket server at the specified port.
syntax_pattern: id of websocket server at port %number%

title: Port of WebSocket
description: An expression for the port, local or external, of the specified websocket.
syntax_pattern:
[the] local port of %websocket%
%websocket%'[s] local port
[the] remote port of %websocket%
%websocket%'[s] remote port
[the] external port of %websocket%
%websocket%'[s] external port

title: Resource Descriptor of Handshake
description: An expression for the resource descriptor of the specified handshake. This can only exist in handshakes sent by the client (ex. 'request' - see the Handshake Request/Response/New expression).
syntax_pattern:
[the] resource descriptor of %handshake%
%handshake%'[s] resource descriptor
[the] handshake resource descriptor of %handshake%
%handshake%'[s] handshake resource descriptor

title: WebSocket Server Port
description: For use under 'websocket server %string%': An expression for the port on which this websocket server is open.

title: Center of Border
description: The center of the specified world's border. This isn't necessarily the same as the spawn.

title: Vectors - Dot Product
description: Gets the dot product between two vectors.

title: Spectator Target
description: Grabs the spectator target entity of the players.

title: Mechanic Responses
description: You can respond to interactions with mechanics using

title: On AdvancedSurvivalGames - Game End
description: Called when a game ends.

title: WorldType of Creator
description: An expression for the worldtype of a creator. This is 'default' by default.

title: All Automatic Creators
description: An expression for all of the world creators that MundoSK is currently set to automatically run on server start.

title: On AdvancedSurvivalGames - Game Start
description: Called when a game starts.

title: On AdvancedSurvivalGames - Item Purchase
description: Called when a player buys an item.

title: On AdvancedSurvivalGames - Kit Purchase
description: Called when a player buys a kit.

title: On AdvancedSurvivalGames - Player Death
description:
Called when a player dies.

**Event Expressions:**
`[the] [advanced] (survival games|sg) victim`
`[the] [advanced] (survival games|sg) (attacker|killer)`

title: On Autorank - Requirement Completion
description: Called when a player completes a requirement.

title: On Cannons - Cannon Create
description: Called when a cannon is created.

title: On Cannons - Cannon Death
description: Called when someone dies from a cannon.

title: On Cannons - Cannon Destroy
description: Called when a cannon is destroyed.

title: On Cannons - Cannon Fire
description: Called when a cannon shoots.

title: On Cannons - Cannon Pre-Creation
description: Called right before a cannon is created.

title: On Cannons - Cannon Use
description: Called when a player interacts with a cannon.

title: On Cannons - Projectile Impact
description: Called when a cannon projectile lands.

title: On CombatLog - Combat Log
description: Called when a player combat logs.

title: On ClearLagg - Clear Entities
description:
Called when ClearLagg cleared entities.

**Event Expressions:**
`[the] entities (cleared|removed|deleted) [by ClearLag[g]]`

title: On ClearLagg - TPS Update
description: Called when ClearLagg TPS is updated.

title: On CombatLog - Tag
description:
Called when a player enters combat.**Event Expressions:**
`[the] [CombatLog] tagged [player]`
`[the] [CombatLog] tagger`

title: On CombatLog - Un-tag
description: Called when a player leaves combat.

title: On GriefPrevention - Claim Expiration
description: Called when a claim expires.

title: LOADER - Plugin
description: Enable/Dispable plugin by name or file

title: PlotSquared | Location in Road
description: Check if a location is in a road
syntax_pattern:
[PlotSquared] %location% is in[side] [the] [plot] road
[PlotSquared] %location% is(n't| not) in[side] [the] [plot] road

title: All Current Worlds
description: An expression for all worlds that are currently loaded. This differs from Skript's 'all worlds' expression in that it still parses as being a list even if there is only one world at the time of parsing.

title: Automatic Creator
description: An expression for the automatic creator (if there is one) that MundoSK is currently set to run for the world with the specified name.
syntax_pattern:
automatic creator %string%
automatic creator for world %string%
automatic creator for world named %string%

title: Citizen Name
description: Returns the name of a citizen. Can be set and reset to its ID.

title: Seed of Creator
description: An expression for the seed of a creator. This isn't necessarily set, in which case a random seed will be used when creating a world using the creator.

title: Citizen Skin
description: Returns the skin name of a citizen. Can be set and reset to "Steve" skin.

title: Citizen Vulnerability
description: Returns the vulnerability of a citizen. Can be set and reset to true.

title: On GriefPrevention - Claim Deletion
description: Called when a claim is deleted.

title: On PrisonMine - Mine Reset Finish
description: Called when a mine is done resetting.

title: BetterModel reload start
description:
Fires when BetterModel is reloading
Use skript-reflect to manipulate with values

title: Citizen from ID
description: Returns a citizen from its ID.

title: PrisonMines - Is Resetting
description: Checks if a mine is currently resetting.
syntax_pattern:
[the] [PrisonMines] mine [(named|with name)] %string% is (resetting|being reset)
[the] [PrisonMines] mine [(named|with name)] %string% is(n't| not) (resetting|being reset)

title: On PrisonMine - Mine Reset Start
description: Called when a mine begins to reset.

title: On Shopkeepers - Create
description: Called when a shopkeeper is created.

title: On Shopkeepers - Delete
description: Called when a shopkeeper is deleted.

title: On Shopkeepers - Trade Complete
description: Called when a shopkeeper trade is completed.

title: On SkyWars (Daboross) - Game End
description:
Called when a game ends.

**Event Expressions:**
`[the] (last|alive|remaining) players [in [the] [SkyWars] game]`

title: On SkyWars (Daboross) - Game Start
description:
Called when a game starts.

**Event Expressions:**
`[the] start[ing] players [in [the] [SkyWars] game]`

title: On SkyWars (Daboross) - Leave Queue
description: Called when a player leaves a game queue.

title: AdvancedBan - Is Banned
description: Checks if a player is banned.
syntax_pattern:
%offlineplayer% is banned [by AdvancedBan]
%offlineplayer% is(n't| not) banned [by AdvancedBan]

title: AdvancedBan - Is Muted
description: Checks if a player is muted.
syntax_pattern:
%offlineplayer% is muted [by AdvancedBan]
%offlineplayer% is(n't| not) muted [by AdvancedBan]

title: AdvancedSurvivalGames - Is Spectating
description: Checks if a player is spectating a game.
syntax_pattern:
%offlineplayer% is spectating [[advanced] (survival games|sg)]
%offlineplayer% is [a[n]] [[advanced] (survival games|sg)] spectator
%offlineplayer% is(n't| not) spectating [[advanced] (survival games|sg)]
%offlineplayer% is(n't| not) [a[n]] [[advanced] (survival games|sg)] spectator

title: Bedwars - Is Game Running
description: Checks if a Bedwars game is running.
syntax_pattern:
[the] [Bedwars] game [(named|with name)] %string% is [currently] (running|active)
[the] [Bedwars] game [(named|with name)] %string% is(n't| not) [currently] (running|active)

title: Bedwars - Is Playing
description: Checks if a player is in a Bedwars game.
syntax_pattern:
%player% is [currently] [playing] in [a] [Bedwars] game
%player% is(n't| not) [currently] [playing] in [a] [Bedwars] game

title: Cannons - Is Cannon Clean
description: Checks if a cannon is clean.
syntax_pattern:
[the] cannon [with ID] %string% is clean[ed]
[the] cannon [with ID] %string% is(n't| not) clean[ed]

title: Cannons - Is Cannon Overheated
description: Checks if a cannon is overheated.
syntax_pattern:
[the] cannon [with ID] %string% is overheated
[the] cannon [with ID] %string% is(n't| not) overheated

title: Cannons - Is Cannon Ready to Fire
description: Checks if a cannon is ready to fire.
syntax_pattern:
[the] cannon [with ID] %string% is ready to (fire|be fired)
[the] cannon [with ID] %string% is(n't| not) ready to (fire|be fired)

title: Cannons - Is Projectile Pushed
description: Checks if the projectile in a cannon has been pushed.
syntax_pattern:
[the] projectile in [the] cannon [with ID] %string% (is|has been) pushed
[the] projectile in [the] cannon [with ID] %string% (is(n't| not)|has(n't| not) been) pushed

title: CombatLog - Is Tagged
description: Checks if a player is combat tagged.

title: LWC - Is Block Protectable
description: Checks if a block is protectable.

title: LWC - Is Block Protected
description: Checks if a block is protected.

title: LWC - Player Access
description: Checks if a player has access to a block.
syntax_pattern:
%player% (has access to|can access) [LWC] [(locked|protected)] %block%
%player% (does(n't| not) have access to|can('t|not) access) [LWC] [(locked|protected)] %block%

title: LockettePro - Is User
description: Checks if a player can use a locked block.
syntax_pattern:
%player% is [a] [LockettePro] user of %block%
%player% is(n't| not) [a] [LockettePro] user of %block%

title: Parties - Is Player in Party
description: Checks if a player is in a party.
syntax_pattern:
%offlineplayer% is in [a] party
%offlineplayer% is(n't| not) in [a] party

title: Parties - Party Exists
description: Checks if a party exists.
syntax_pattern:
[a] party [(named|with name)] %string% exists
[a] party [(named|with name)] %string% does(n't| not) exists

title: PlotSquared - Is Player in Plot
description: Checks if a player is in a plot.
syntax_pattern:
%player% is [currently] in [a] [PlotSquared] plot
%player% is(n't| not) [currently] in [a] [PlotSquared] plot

title: SkyWars (CookLoco) - Is Spectating
description: Checks if a player is spectating.
syntax_pattern:
%player% is [currently] spectating [a] SkyWars [game]
%player% is [currently] [a] [SkyWars] spectator
%player% is(n't| not) [currently] spectating [a] SkyWars [game]
%player% is(n't| not) [currently] [a] [SkyWars] spectator

title: Entity Citizen
description: Returns the citizen of an entity. Cannot be changed.

title: Last Created Citizen
description: Returns the last created citizen.

title: SkyWars (Daboross) - Is Queue Full
description: Checks if the game queue is full.
syntax_pattern:
[the] [SkyWars] [game] queue is full
[the] [SkyWars] [game] queue is(n't| not) full

title: Bedwars - Join Game
description: Forces a player to join a Bedwars game.
syntax_pattern:
make %player% join [the] [Bedwars] game [(named|with name)] %string%
force %player% to join [the] [Bedwars] game [(named|with name)] %string%

title: Bedwars - Leave Game
description: Forces a player to leave a Bedwars game.
syntax_pattern:
make %player% leave [the] [Bedwars] game [(named|with name)] %string%
force %player% to leave [the] [Bedwars] game [(named|with name)] %string%

title: Bedwars - Start Game
description: Starts a Bedwars game.

title: Bedwars - Stop Game
description: Stops a Bedwars game.

title: Cannons - Fire Cannon
description: Fires a cannon.

title: LWC - Remove Protection
description: Removes protection from a block.

title: LockettePro - Lock Block
description: Locks a block by placing a sign on it.

title: MinePacks - Add Item
description: Adds item to backpack of player.

title: MinePacks - Remove Item
description: Removes item from backpack of player.

title: Parties - Add Player to Party
description: Adds a player to a party.

title: Parties - Create Party
description: Creates a party.

title: PrisonMines - Reset Mine
description: Resets a mine.

title: Shopkeepers - Delete Shopkeeper
description: Delete a shopkeeper.

title: SkyWars (Daboross) - Add Player to Queue
description: Adds a player to the game queue.

title: SkyWars (Daboross) - Remove Player from Queue
description: Removes a player from the game queue.

title: AdvancedBan - Ban Reason
description: Returns the ban reason of a player.

title: AdvancedBan - Banner
description: Returns the banner of a player.

title: AdvancedBan - Mute Reason
description: Returns the mute reason of a player.

title: AdvancedBan - Mute Time
description: Returns the mute time of a player.
syntax_pattern:
[the] remaining [AdvancedBan] mute time of %offlineplayer%
%offlineplayer%'s remaining [AdvancedBan] mute time

title: AdvancedBan - Muter
description: Returns the muter of a player.

title: AdvancedBan - Punish Duration
description: Returns the punish duration on Punishment event.

title: AdvancedBan - Punished Player
description: Returns the punished player on Punishment event.

title: AdvancedBan - Punisher
description:
Returns the punisher on Punishment event.
**Note:** Return type of this expression is string because the punisher can be console.

title: AdvancedBan - Punishment Reason
description: Returns the punish reason on Punishment event.

title: AdvancedBan - Punishment Type
description: Returns the punish type on Punishment event.

title: AdvancedBan - Punishments
description: Returns the active punishments of a player.

title: AdvancedBan - Remaining Ban Time

title: Create Blueprint
description: Creates a blueprint and puts it in the specified variable (the %object% at the end). This is a delayed effect as it requires retrieving image data either from online or from a file, so if used inside of a function the function will return before the effect (and any code after the effect) completes. The first syntax creates the blueprint from an existing skin. The second syntax creates from an image at the specified url or file path. If the blueprint is meant to be a blueprint of a certain part of a skin (ex. the head, right leg, etc.), a part in the second layer of a skin, or even a certain face (front, back, top, etc.) of a part, you can specify that. You can also specify whether it is meant to be a slim skin (skin with thinner arms).
syntax_pattern:
create blueprint of %skin% in %object%

title: WebSocket Server Template
description:
Not an actual event, but rather a template for a websocket server, with the specified ID. Under the main "event" line you can have seven different sub-scopes that handle websocket events:
on start: This is called when the websocket server is started.
on stop: This is called when the websocket server is stopped.
on handshake: This is called before 'on open', when a client has sent a request handshake, allowing you to modify the response handshake to be sent as well as verify that the client's request is valid, and refuse the request if you deem it to be invalid. Note that you can't send messages to the client at this point.
on open: This is called when a client opens a websocket connection with this websocket server.
on message: This is called when the other end of a websocket connection sends a message.
on error: This is called when an error occurs related to a websocket connection.
on close: This is called when a websocket connection is closed.

title: Call Custom Event
description: Calls a custom event with the specified id and optionally the specified details and/or arguments. Details are used in events as event-type. For example, if you had a detail 3426, event-number would equal 3426. Details may be of any type that is in Skript by default (number, string, player, world, etc.) as well as of any type added in MundoSK (creator, achievement, difficulty, etc.), and possibly other addons, depending on what loads in what order. You can't have two or more details of the same type. If you try to do this, only the detail that comes last of that type will be used. Arguments are like details, except that you may have multiple arguments of the same type, and they can be of any type from any addon. Arguments are accessed from within the event using the Args of Custom Event expression. For both details and arguments, you have to put them in a list variable and then call the custom event using the list variable in the syntax, otherwise you'll get an internal error. In MundoSK 1.8, two new features have been introduced (these will not work in previous versions):First, you can specify that the custom event is being called asynchronously. When code running in async is calling a custom event, this should be specified in order to prevent errors and corruption. Second, you can specify multiple custom event ids. This allows users of your custom events to choose from a variety of possible ids to list for custom events. Note that you must specify at least one id, otherwise no event will be called.

title: Enable or Disable Array Tablist
description: Enables or disables the array tablist for the specified player(s). The array tablist creates a grid of tabs that allows you to use grid coordinates to easily modify individual tabs. When enabling, you can specify the amount of columns (defaults to 4), the amount of rows (defaults to 20), and the initial icon (defaults to a white texture). See the Size of Array Tablist and Icon of Array Tabl expressions for more info. If the array tablist is already enabled, it will be replaced with a blank one matching the new specifications. Note that when enabling the array tablist, all simple tabs will be removed and all player tabs will be hidden. When disabling the array tablist, initially either all player tabs will be hidden, or (if if the array tablist was 4x20) all player tabs will be visible. There will be no simple tabs either way initially after disabling the array tablist.
syntax_pattern:
(disable|deactivate) array tablist for %players%
(enable|activate) array tablist for %players% [with [%-number% columns] [%-number% rows] [initial (head|icon|skull) %-skin%]]

title: ListUtil General
description: ListUtil is a general set of expressions and effects used for manipulating lists. Each ListUtil effect/expression provides a certain functionality for lists in general, and contains '%listutil%' somewhere in its syntax - listutil isn't an actual type, but instead allows you to input a sort of "specifier" as to how you want to provide the list that is going to be manipulated. ListUtil effects/expressions also have an '%objects%' in their syntax from which the list is going to be gotten. The listutil specifier described by the above syntax is used for manipulating all lists, meaning you can write 'elem' where '%listutil%' is and input any list in '%objects%' to manipulate it. For example, using the Element of List expression, you could write 'elem 3 of {_list::*}' and that would be the third element of the list variable.See the Book ListUtil expression as another example

title: Tree Loop
description: An expression meant to only be used in loops, that allows you to loop through all of the indexes and values of the specified list variable, including the sub-indexes and sub-values. For example, if you do 'set {_temp::pie::1} to "ex" in Skript, looping through {_temp::*} will ignore that value. However, the tree loop allows you to loop through all possible values contained inside the specified list variable. Make sure to also see the Branch expression. Note: before MundoSK 1.8, modifying the list variable while looping through its tree sometimes caused errors. As of MundoSK 1.8, this will not cause errors. Instead, these modifications will be ignored during the tree loop.

title: JSON Field of Packet
description: An expression for certain fields of packets (first see the Packet Info expression for a more general explanation) that don't have equivalent types in Skript, and thus must be represented in the form of a jsonobject. The names of the fields can be written as strings but don't have to be as of MundoSK 1.8. Current accept JSON infos: 'chatcomponent', 'serverping', 'datawatcher', 'watchablecollection', 'gameprofile', 'nbt', 'chatcomponent' array, 'playerinfodata' array.

title: Loop While
description: An expression used in loops in order to loop through a list of objects either while or until a certain boolean expression is true. SkQuery's 'check %predicate%' expression can be used to use a condition as the boolean expression. If 'while' or 'until' are used, then the expression will cause the loop to loop infinitely, repeating the objects once the end is reached, until the boolean expression changes. However, if 'if' or 'unless' are used, then the loop will terminate once all objects are looped through.

title: When Boolean is True
description:
Not an effect, but rather a scope (written with a colon at the end with a section of indented code under it, like an if statement or loop). 
A scope that waits until the specified boolean expression is true, then executes the block of code under it. The lines of code that come after the scope execute immediately, rather than waiting for the boolean expression to be true. SkQuery's 'check %predicate%' expression can be used to use a condition as the boolean expression. Optionally, you can specify a timespan to be the interval to wait between checking the boolean expression. This is 1 tick by default.

title: Overlay Blueprint on Blueprint
description: Overlays the first specified blueprint on the second specified blueprint. To understand what "overlay" means, you can imagine the blueprints being pieces of paper (possibly with transparency), and just putting one piece of paper on top of the other. So if the first specified blueprint is fully opaque, then it will completely replace the second specified blueprint, which is sometimes what you need. Note that the overlaying is done by matching the top left corner of both blueprints, so if the first specified blueprint is smaller than the second, then the lower and or the right pixels of the second specified blueprint won't have anything overlayed on them.

title: HOLOGRAM - Update (BETA)
description: Update hologram

title: Array Tablist is Enabled
description: Checks whether the array tablist is enabled or disabled for the specified players. See the Enable or Disable Array Tablist effect for more info.

title: Recolor Blueprint
description: Recolors all pixels with the first specified color in the specified blueprint as having the second specified color.

title: Indices of List
description: Gets indices of a list variable.

title: On Log
description: This is called when a message is sent in console. Note that using broadcast on the on log event will infinitely loop.

title: Make Say
description: Forces a player to send a message to the chat. If the message starts with a slash it will force the player to use command.

title: Blocks in Region
description:
All blocks in a region.
This expression requires a supported regions plugin to be installed.

title: Language
description:
Currently selected game language of a player. The value of the language is not defined properly.
The vanilla Minecraft client will use lowercase language / country pairs separated by an underscore, but custom resource packs may use any format they wish.

title: Map State
description: represents a state of a map that can be sent to the player to display changes on a map, useful as it is faster than drawing images often on a map

title: BetterModel reload end
description: Fires when BetterModel reload finishes

title: Group Score Value
description:
These expressions will get either the name or value of a group based score.

For more details on how to use the skRayFall Scoreboard/Sidebar system, a tutorial can be found [here](https://skripthub.net/tutorials/19).
syntax_pattern:
group score (name|title) (of|from) id %string%
group score (value|number) (of|from) id %string%

title: Async in Timespan
description:
Not an effect, but rather a scope (written with a colon at the end with a section of indented code under it, like an if statement or loop). 
A scope used to run a certain block of code asynchronously. This means that the code will be run on a separate thread from the main server thread, allowing you to perform tasks such as making web requests without lagging the server. Optionally, you can specify a timespan to wait before running the block of code. The lines of code following the scope will run as normal without waiting for any of the block of code to start/finish. It is also possible to write this scope as a regular line of code, in which case instead of a block of code below a scope, all following lines of code will be forced to run asynchronously, as well as wait a certain timespan if it is specified.

title: Level of Enchantment within Enchanted Book
description: An expression for the level of the specified enchantment in the specified enchantment book. This is 0 if the specified book does not contain the specified enchantment.

title: Last Logged Message
description: Returns the last logged message

title: On Path Finish
description: Fires when an active pathfind reaches its destination.

title: Displayed Skin of Player
description: An expression for the skin currently being displayed as the specified player's skin. If target ('for') players are specified, the expression will return a skin for each target player specified. Excluded players are meant to be specified only when setting the expression (for example, to prevent the original specified player from seeing a change). If the expression is evaluated with excluded players specified, it will act the same as if no target or excluded players had been specified.

title: Size of Array Tablist
description:
An expression for the amount of rows or columns in the array tablist. There can be 1 to 4 columns.For each amount of columns, there is a specified range for the amount of rows:
1 Column: 1 to 20 rows
2 Columns: 11 to 20 rows
3 Columns: 14 to 20 rows
4 Columns: 16 to 20 rows
This is due to the fact that Minecraft allows 1 to 80 total tabs, and for each amount, there is only one way the tablist can appear. Minecraft only allows a maximum of 20 tabs in one column, so the tabs will try to fill as few columns as possible will adhering to this rule. For example, if there are 40 tabs, this is satisfied by a 2x20 tablist, but for 41 and 42 you need 3x14.

title: HTTP Status of Handshake
description: An expression for the HTTP status of the specified handshake. This can only exist in handshakes sent by the server (ex. 'response' - see the Handshake Request/Response/New expression).
syntax_pattern:
[the] http status of %handshake%
%handshake%'[s] http status
[the] handshake http status of %handshake%
%handshake%'[s] handshake http status

[the] warp[s] [with] [name][s] %strings% (of|from) [the] [faction] %conquerfaction% (doesn't| does not|don't|do not) (use|has) (a password|authentication)

title: Blank Blueprint
description: A new, blank blueprint. All pixels are colored transparent by default, which for the first layer means that they will render as black (but still act as transparent when using blueprint syntaxes).If the blueprint is meant to be a blueprint of a certain part of a skin (ex. the head, right leg, etc.), a part in the second layer of a skin, or even a certain face (front, back, top, etc.) of a part, you can specify that. You can also specify whether it is meant to be a slim skin (skin with thinner arms).

description: The cosine function. This is basically the sine shifted by 90°, i.e. cos(a) = sin(a + 90°), for any number a. Uses degrees, not radians.

title: Priority of Simple Tab
description: This is the priority of the specified simple tab in the specified or all tablist(s). The priority is a string (at most 12 characters) that determines the position that the specified simple tab will take relative to the other simple tabs. Specifically, simple tabs are arranged alphabetically by their priority. By default the priority is the first 12 characters of the simple tab's id.

title: ARGB Color
description: A color that can have transparency; 'rgb' stands for the usual red, green, blue values (from 0 to 255 inclusive), and 'a' stands for the alpha value that describes transparency, where 0 means fully transparent, and 255 means fully opaque. When using normal Skript colors (green, blue, etc.) as argb colors, they will be converted as fully opaque. You can also write argb colors as hex codes: `rgb RRGGBB` will be a fully opaque argb color from the hex code RRGGBB, and `argb AARRGGBB` will be an argb colors with transparency AA and rgb hex code RRGGBB.

title: Blueprint
description: A blueprint of a skin that can be modified in Skript and then used to create an actual skin that you can put on players. A blueprint could be for a whole skin or be a section of another blueprint.

title: On Vault Request - Create Account (Return: boolean)
description: Called when Vault requests a player economy account to be created

title: abs
description: Returns the absolute value of the argument, i.e. makes the argument positive.

title: Vectors - Cross Product
description: Gets the cross product between two vectors.

title: atan
description: The inverse of the tangent, also called arctan. Returns result in degrees, not radians. Only returns values from -90 to 90.

title: atan2
description:
Similar to atan, but requires two coordinates and returns values from -180 to 180.
The returned angle is measured counterclockwise in a standard mathematical coordinate system (x to the right, y to the top).

title: Logged Message
description: Returns the logged message in a log event.

title: acos
description: The inverse of the cosine, also called arccos. Returns result in degrees, not radians. Only returns values from 0 to 180.

title: asin
description: The inverse of the sine, also called arcsin. Returns result in degrees, not radians. Only returns values from -90 to 90.

title: PlayerPoints - Balance
description: Returns the PlayerPoints balance of a player.
