title: Dust Transition
description:
Creates a new dust transition to be used with 'dust_color_transition' particle.
Color can either be a regular color or an RGB color using Skript's rgb() function.
Size is the size the particle will be (limited between 0.01 and 4.0).
syntax_pattern: dustTransition(fromColor: color, toColor: color, size: number)

title: ItemComponent - Swing Animation Component Apply
description:
Specifies the swing animation to play when attacking or interacting using this item.
See [**Attack Animation Component**](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Data_component_format#attack_animation) and [**Interact Animation Component**](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Data_component_format#interact_animation) on McWiki for more details.
Requires Minecraft 26.3+

**ENTRIES**:
All entries are optional and will use their defaults when omitted.
- `type` = String, The type of swinging animation. Can be "none", "whack", "stab". Defaults to "whack".
- `duration` = A timespan that determines the animation's duration. Defaults to 6 ticks.
entries: [{"name": "type", "isRequired": false, "isSection": false}, {"name": "duration", "isRequired": false, "isSection": false}]

title: Pathfind
description:
Moves an entity toward a location or another entity over a specified duration.
Supports easing for smoother movement and optional sideways sine-wave wobble.
When targeting another entity, the path follows that entity as it moves.
Fires 'on path finish' when the destination is reached, or 'on path cancel' when interrupted.

Easing options: linear, ease_in, ease_out, ease_in_out, bounce.
Wobble is measured in blocks.
syntax_pattern:
pathfind %entity% to %entity% over %number% seconds [with easing %string%] [wobble %number%]
pathfind %entity% to %location% over %number% seconds [with easing %string%] [wobble %number%]

title: Evaluate Math Formula
description:
Evaluates an advanced math formula and returns a number.
Supports arithmetic (+ - * / ^ %), parentheses, and:
abs, min, max, floor, ceil, sqrt, cbrt, pow,
sin, cos, tan, cot, asin, acos, atan,
sinh, cosh, tanh,
ln, log, log10, log2, log1p,
exp, expm1, signum.

Placeholders available inside the formula:
<entity.x>, <entity.y>, <entity.z>, <entity.health>, <entity.max_health>,
<bone.position.NAME.x/y/z>, <bone.rotation.NAME.x/y/z>,
<bone.scale.NAME>, and <var.NAME>.

<var.NAME> reads a numeric Skript variable using the current Skript event context.
The formula is evaluated synchronously after placeholders are resolved.
No 'run async:' wrapper is needed.

title: Evaluate Math Formula (Vector)
description:
Evaluates three math formulas for X, Y and Z and returns them as a single Vector.
Uses the same formula functions and placeholders as 'evaluate ... for ...'.
Each component may contain its own formula.

title: Path Progress
description:
Returns the current progress of an entity's active pathfind as a number from 0 to 1.
Returns 0 when the entity does not currently have an active pathfind.

title: On Unknown Command Execution
description: Called when a player executes an unknown command.

title: Changed Sign Side
description: Checks whether a side was changed in a sign change event.
syntax_pattern:
[the] (front|back) [side] (is|was) changed
[the] (front|back) [side] (is not|isn't|was not|wasn't) changed
[the] changed side (is|was) [the] (front|back)
[the] changed side (is not|isn't|was not|wasn't) [the] (front|back)

title: Is Charged
description:
Checks if a creeper, wither, or wither skull is charged (powered).
Please note that it is not possible to change whether a wither is charged.

title: Is a Script Command
description: Checks whether a command (string label) is a script command (one registered in a script).

title: Command
description:
Executes a command. This can be useful to use other plugin in triggers.
If the command is a BungeeCord side command, you can use the '[bungeecord]' keyword option to execute the command on the proxy.
syntax_pattern:
execute [the] [bungee[cord]] command[s] %strings% [by %commandsenders%]
execute [the] %commandsenders% [bungee[cord]] command[s] %strings%
(let|make) %commandsenders% execute [[the] [bungee[cord]] command[s]] %strings%

title: Execute Raw Query
description: Runs a SQL query and stores its rows under one-based indexes and column labels, such as {_rows::1::name}. Use with to bind values to ? placeholders. The SQL is sent as written: registered table definitions are not checked, and no database-specific translation is applied. This form does not accept a where block or work with command-based databases.
syntax_pattern: execute query %string% [with %objects%] and store [the] [result] in %objects% [and wait]

title: Execute Raw Update
description: Runs a SQL statement such as ALTER TABLE or UPDATE. Use with to bind values to ? placeholders. You can store the affected-row count reported by the database; statements without a count report 0. The SQL is sent as written, without checking registered tables or translating it for the database. It does not work with command-based databases. Check last database error for failures.
syntax_pattern: execute update %string% [with %objects%] [and store affected rows in %number%] [and wait]

title: Create Database Connection
description: Opens a database connection and waits until it is ready. An unnamed connection replaces the default; a named connection leaves existing connections in place. The first successful connection also becomes the default. The url property is required; username and password may be empty. Other literal properties are passed to the database implementation. On failure, check last database error.
syntax_pattern:
create [a] connection named %string% to [database] %string% [with properties]
create [a] connection to [database] %string% [with properties]

title: Insert Many Entities
description: Inserts multiple rows. Each block under values describes one row; alternatively, supply a list variable in select-result format. Large variables are read across ticks, then written in batches. Keep the source variable unchanged until the insert finishes. The next line runs after the insert finishes. Check last database error for failures or store affected rows for the reported count.
syntax_pattern:
insert many [entities] into [table] %string% [and store affected rows in %number%] [and wait]
insert many [entities] %objects% into [table] %string% [and store affected rows in %number%] [and wait]

title: Argument
description:
A user provided value in a command execution.
For example, if the command "/tell <player> <text>" is used like "/tell Njol Hello Njol!", 'argument 1' is the player named "Njol" and 'argument 2' is the text "Hello Njol!".
One can also use the type of the argument instead of its index to address the argument.
For example, in the command example above, 'player-argument' is the same as 'argument 1'.
Usable in script commands and command events.
Please note that specifying the argument type is only supported in script commands.
syntax_pattern:
[the] last arg[ument]
[the] arg[ument](-| )<(\d+)>
[the] (first|second|third|<(\d*1)st|(\d*2)nd|(\d*3)rd|(\d*[4-90])th>) arg[ument][s]
[all [[of] the]|the] arg[ument][s]
[the] %*classinfo%( |-)arg[ument][( |-)<\d+>]
[the] arg[ument]( |-)%*classinfo%[( |-)<\d+>]

title: Choice Argument
description:
Represents the literal argument out of a choice group selected by the command sender.
Choice arguments, just like regular arguments, are numbered in order of occurrence (left to right).
This expression also supports optional literal arguments.
syntax_pattern:
[the] choice arg[ument] <(\d+)>
[the] (first|second|third|<(\d*1)st|(\d*2)nd|(\d*3)rd|(\d*[4-90])th>) choice arg[ument][s]
[the] [last] choice arg[ument]

title: Command
description: The command that caused an 'on command' event (excluding the leading slash and all arguments)

title: Command Executor
description:
The executor of a command.
This differs from the command sender in that the executor may not be the thing that triggered/initiated the command.
The executor of a command is often changed to be different from the command sender by using a vanilla command such as "/execute".

title: Command Info
description: Get information about a command.
syntax_pattern:
[the] main command [label|name] [of [[the] command[s]] %strings%]
command[s] %strings%'[s] main command [label|name]
[the] description [of [[the] command[s]] %strings%]
command[s] %strings%'[s] description
[the] label [of [[the] command[s]] %strings%]
command[s] %strings%'[s] label
[the] usage [of [[the] command[s]] %strings%]
command[s] %strings%'[s] usage
[all [[of] the]|the] aliases [of [[the] command[s]] %strings%]
command[s] %strings%'[s] aliases
[the] permission [of [[the] command[s]] %strings%]
command[s] %strings%'[s] permission
[the] permission message [of [[the] command[s]] %strings%]
command[s] %strings%'[s] permission message
[the] plugin [owner] [of [[the] command[s]] %strings%]
command[s] %strings%'[s] plugin [owner]

title: Item Model
description: The item model of an item. Accepts a Namespaced Key which takes the form of "namespace:key", e.g. "minecraft:dirt". See  this article for more detail.

title: Item Rarity
description: The item rarity of an item.

title: Item With Model
description: Returns a copy of an item with a custom item model. Accepts a Namespaced Key which takes the form of "namespace:key", e.g. "minecraft:dirt". See  this article for more detail.

title: Script Command Cooldown Information
description:
Only usable in script commands.
Represents the cooldown time, the cooldown bypass permission, the remaining cooldown time, the elapsed cooldown time.
syntax_pattern:
[the] ((cooldown|wait) time|[wait] time of [the] (cooldown|wait) [(of|for) [the] [current] command])
[the] [cooldown] bypass perm[ission] [of [the] (cooldown|wait) [(of|for) [the] [current] command]]
[the] remaining [time] [of [the] (cooldown|wait) [(of|for) [the] [current] command]]
[the] elapsed [time] [of [the] (cooldown|wait) [(of|for) [the] [current] command]]

title: Script Command Suggestion Input
description:
Usable in a script command's "suggestions" entry.
This provides information including the full content of what the player has typed so far, what they have typed as part of the current argument, and at what position within the full content the current argument starts (starting from 1).
syntax_pattern:
[the] [command] [suggestion|tab completion] (full|complete) input
[the] [command] [suggestion|tab completion] (current|arg[ument]) input
[the] [command] [suggestion|tab completion] (current|arg[ument]) input [start[ing]] (position|index)

title: Script Command Suggestions
description:
Usable in a script command's "suggestions" entry.
Allows modifying the suggestions displayed while a command is being typed.

title: Sign Text
description: A line of text on a sign. Can be changed, but note that there is a 16 character limit per line. If a sign side is not specified, the front side will be used by default, unless in a sign change event and a block is not explicitly specified.

title: Locally Suppress Warning
description: Suppresses target warnings from the current script.
syntax_pattern:
[local[ly]] [un]suppress [the] (conflict|variable save|[missing] conjunction|starting [with] expression[s]|variable[ name][s] contain[s|ing] colon[s]|deprecated syntax|unreachable code|constant condition[s]) warning[s]
[start|stop] [local[ly]] suppressing [the] (conflict|variable save|[missing] conjunction|starting [with] expression[s]|variable[ name][s] contain[s|ing] colon[s]|deprecated syntax|unreachable code|constant condition[s]) warning[s]

title: Suppress Type Hints (Experimental)
description:
An effect to suppress local variable type hint errors for the syntax lines that follow this effect.
NOTE: Suppressing type hints also prevents syntax from providing new type hints. For example, with type hints suppressed, 'set {_x} to true' would not provide 'boolean' as a type hint for '{_x}'
syntax_pattern:
[un]suppress [local variable] type hints
(start|stop) suppressing [local variable] type hints

title: Delete Entities Without A Colon
description: Deletes all rows allowed by the database implementation, optionally up to a positive limit. Use this form without a colon when there is no where block. The next line runs after the delete finishes. Check last database error for failures or store affected rows for the reported count.
syntax_pattern: delete [entities] from [table] %string% [with limit %integer%] [and store affected rows in %number%] [and wait]

title: Execute Raw Command
description: Runs a JSON command on a document database and stores the response document. The command is sent as written, without checking registered tables or binding parameters. It does not work with SQL connections.
syntax_pattern: execute command %string% and store [the] [result] in %objects% [and wait]

title: Use Database Connection
description: Uses a named connection for the rest of the current event. The change takes effect immediately. An unknown or disconnected name leaves the current connection unchanged and sets last database error. An in connection section still uses its own connection.

title: Delete Entities
description: Deletes rows matching an optional where block. Without a filter, it deletes all rows allowed by the database implementation. A positive limit may restrict the number deleted. The next line runs after the delete finishes; check last database error for failures or store affected rows for the reported count.
syntax_pattern: delete [entities] from [table] %string% [with limit %integer%] [and store affected rows in %number%] [and wait]

title: On API Request
description:
Fires when the built-in HTTP/HTTPS server receives a valid API request.
Event value: 'event-apirequest' (the request, which can be answered with the 'reply to' effect).

title: On Block Change Packet
description:
Fires whenever a block update packet is sent to a player (block placed or broken, natural updates, or a fake block sent with 'make player see block as ...'). Cancelling removes the block from the packet, so only cancel it after checking the block. The event is asynchronous when the packet is sent off the main thread.
Event values: 'event-player' (the receiver), 'event-location', 'event-blockdata' (the block data sent in the packet) and 'event-block' (the real block currently at the location, not what the packet sends). This event can be cancelled.

title: On Vote Event
description:
Fires when a player votes for the server on a voting site (received through Votifier/NuVotifier).
Event values (all strings): 'event-vote username' (or 'voter'), 'event-vote service' (or 'voting service'), 'event-vote address' (or 'voter address'), 'event-vote timestamp' (or 'vote time').
event_values: event-vote address, event-vote service, event-vote time, event-vote timestamp, event-vote username, event-voter, event-voter address, event-voting service

title: [Navigation] Has Real Entity
description: Checks if one or more fakes navigations are using real entities.
syntax_pattern:
%navigations% (has|have) [a] real entit(y|ies)
%navigations% (has|have)(n't| not) [a] real entit(y|ies)
%navigations% (do|does)(n't| not) have [a] real entit(y|ies)

title: Send Advancement Notification
description: Sends a task, goal, or challenge advancement toast to players using packets only. The advancement is hidden from advancement tabs and never produces a chat message.
syntax_pattern:
send task notification with item %itemstack% title %string% to %players%
send goal notification with item %itemstack% title %string% to %players%
send challenge notification with item %itemstack% title %string% to %players%

title: [API] Reply To Request
description: Sends an HTTP response to an API request. Optionally specify a status code (default 200).
syntax_pattern:
reply to %apirequest% with %string%
reply to %apirequest% with code %number% and %string%

title: [ChunkPath] Delete Chunk Path
description: Deletes the chunk path record of a chunk (from memory and from the world's chunk path database), if any. Does nothing if that chunk was never registered.

title: [ChunkPath] Register Chunk Path
description: Analyzes a chunk and (re)registers its chunk path record (its gates to neighboring chunks) in the world's chunk path database. Unlike a normal lookup, this always re-runs the analysis and overwrites any record already saved for that chunk. The chunk must already be generated on disk (never generates it). Optionally accepts one or more custom path cost rules (built via 'a new path cost rule') to use for this analysis instead of the world's default cost rules. This can be a heavy operation on the calling thread — avoid registering many chunks at once from the main thread.

title: [Long Navigation] Destroy Navigation
description: Destroys one or more long navigation instances, removing them from the global tick registry. Once destroyed, the navigating object stops moving and its tick() method will no longer be called. Always destroy long navigation instances when they are no longer needed to avoid memory leaks.

title: Body Yaw
description: Gets the body yaw rotation of a player (read-only).

title: Display Background Color
description: Gets or sets the background color of a text display entity using Skript's color type. Alpha is preserved. Targets can be one or more displays or a display group.
syntax_pattern:
[the] fake display background [color] of %displaydata/displaygroup%
[the] fake display background [color] of %displaydatas/displaygroups%

title: Display Block Data
description: Gets or sets the block data of block displays. Targets can be one or more displays or a display group.
syntax_pattern:
[the] fake display block[ ]data of %displaydata/displaygroup%
[the] fake display block[ ]data of %displaydatas/displaygroups%

title: Group Transformation
description: Gets or sets the center, translation, rotation, or scale of a display group. Center and translation return a Vector; rotation returns a Quaternionf; scale returns a Number.
syntax_pattern:
[the] group center of %displaygroup%
[the] group translation of %displaygroup%
[the] group rotation of %displaygroup%
[the] group scale of %displaygroup%

title: Matched Group
description: A capture group (by index or by name) of the current match in a 'replace regex ... with code' section. Group 0 is the whole matched text. Cannot be changed.

title: Matched Text
description: The text matched by the regex in the current iteration of a 'replace regex ... with code' section. Cannot be changed.

title: Previous Last Format
description:
In a 'replace regex ... with code' section, the MiniMessage tags (colors and decorations) that are active at the end of the text placed before the current match, replacements already made included.
Add it after '<reset>' at the end of a replacement to give the following text the format it had before the match. Click, hover and insertion are not included. Empty when no format is active.

title: Replaced Text
description:
The text that will replace the current match at the end of the iteration of a 'replace regex ... with code' section.
Defaults to the matched text. Can be set, deleted (removes the match) or reset (back to the matched text).

title: [ChunkPath] All Chunk Paths
description: Returns every chunk path record already registered for a world, read directly from its database. Never triggers an analysis by itself — use 'register chunk path of %chunk%' for that. Returns nothing if no chunk has ever been registered for that world.

title: [ChunkPath] Chunk
description: Returns the actual chunk a chunk path record was computed for. Read-only. May load the chunk if it isn't currently loaded. Returns nothing if that world is no longer loaded.

title: [ChunkPath] Chunk Path Record
description: Returns the chunk path record already registered for a chunk (its analyzed gates), or nothing if that chunk has never been registered. Never triggers an analysis by itself — use 'register chunk path of %chunk%' for that.

title: [ChunkPath] Gate Path Locations
description: Computes the shortest chunk-to-chunk gate path between two locations and returns the representative location of every gate crossed along the way, in order (start -> end). Reuses only chunk path records already known/analyzed for the crossed chunks: a gate leading to a chunk that was never registered is treated as a dead end and ignored, it never triggers a chunk analysis by itself. Returns nothing if the two locations aren't in the same world, if either isn't on/near practicable ground, or if no path could be found.

title: [ChunkPath] Linked Chunks
description: Returns every neighboring chunk connected to at least one gate of a chunk path record (i.e. chunks reachable from it according to the chunk-to-chunk analysis), as a list of chunks. Read-only. May load those chunks if they aren't currently loaded. Records whose world is no longer loaded are silently skipped.

title: [ChunkPath] Locations
description: Returns block locations extracted from one or more chunk path records, in a form native to Skript (a list of locations): the representative point of every gate, every single border block belonging to a gate, or only the representative points of gates still considered dead ends. Read-only. Records whose world is no longer loaded are silently skipped.
syntax_pattern:
gate locations of chunk path %chunkpathrecord%
border block locations of chunk path %chunkpathrecord%
dead end gate locations of chunk path %chunkpathrecord%

title: [ChunkPath] Numeric Properties
description: Gets numeric properties of a chunk path record: its chunk X/Z coordinates, or its gate count. Read-only.
syntax_pattern:
chunk x of chunk path %chunkpathrecord%
chunk z of chunk path %chunkpathrecord%
gate count of chunk path %chunkpathrecord%

title: [ChunkPath] Path Cost Rule Blocks
description: Gets, sets, adds to, removes from, or clears the list of exact blocks matched by a path cost rule (the rule's cost applies to a chunk position when its floor block is one of these blocks, or tagged by one of its tags). 'set'/'add'/'remove' accept a material, a physical block, an item stack, or an item type — all of them are converted to (and stored as) a plain material, exactly like before. Giving an item that can't exist as a placed block (e.g. a snowball) logs a console warning since it will then never match a chunk's floor block. 'delete' and 'reset' both empty the list; the rule's cost itself is untouched by either.

title: [ChunkPath] Path Cost Rule Cost
description: Gets or sets the movement cost applied by a path cost rule when one of its blocks/tags matches. The cost is a whole number: a decimal value is rounded to the nearest integer (2.5 gives 3). Unlike the rule's blocks/tags lists, this does not support 'add', 'remove', 'delete', or 'reset' — only get and set.

title: [ChunkPath] Path Cost Rule Creation
description: Creates a new, empty path cost rule (no blocks/tags yet), optionally with an initial cost (0 if omitted; a whole number, decimals are rounded). Populate it with 'blocks of path cost rule %pathcostrules%' and 'tags of path cost rule %pathcostrules%', then pass one or more rules to 'register chunk path of %chunk% using rules %pathcostrules%'.
syntax_pattern: a new path cost rule [with cost %number%]

title: [ChunkPath] Path Cost Rule Tags
description: Gets, sets, adds to, removes from, or clears the list of block tags matched by a path cost rule (e.g. 'minecraft tag "leaves"' — the "minecraft" namespace is assumed unless one is given). One or several tags can be given at once to 'add', 'remove' and 'set'. Tags that no longer resolve to a known block tag are simply ignored when the rule is used, never an error. 'delete' and 'reset' both empty the list; the rule's cost itself is untouched by either.

title: [ChunkPath] World
description: Returns the world a chunk path record belongs to. Read-only. Returns nothing if that world is no longer loaded.

title: [Long Navigation] Creation
description: Creates a new long-distance navigation object. Can be created from a numeric entity ID or a real entity. Requires a hitbox vector (width/height) and a starting location for the virtual pattern; only a speed is optional. Unlike a normal navigation, there is no movement type: long navigations are always ground-based. It will not start moving until an end location is set (see 'end location of').
syntax_pattern:
[a] [new] long navigation with id %number% hitbox %vector% location %location% [speed %number%] [with players %players%]
[a] [new] long navigation with entity %entity% [speed %number%]

title: [Long Navigation] Entity
description: Returns the real Bukkit entity attached to a long navigation object. Returns nothing if the long navigation was created from a numeric ID rather than a real entity.
syntax_pattern:
entity of long navigation %longnavigation%
long navigation %longnavigation%'s entity

title: [Long Navigation] Locations
description: Gets or sets the start location, end location (destination), or current location of a long navigation object. Setting the start or end location (re)computes the chunk-gate route; setting the current location teleports the underlying entity (or virtual position) directly, like 'location of navigation'.
syntax_pattern:
start location of long navigation %longnavigation%
(end location|destination) of long navigation %longnavigation%
[current] location of long navigation %longnavigation%

title: [Long Navigation] Numeric Properties
description: Gets or sets numeric properties of a long navigation object: movement speed, pause duration in ticks, or the numeric entity ID (read-only).
syntax_pattern:
speed of long navigation %longnavigation%
pause ticks of long navigation %longnavigation%
entity id of long navigation %longnavigation%

title: [Long Navigation] Status
description: Returns the current status of a long navigation, as lowercase text: "idle" (no route yet), "following" (walking toward the current waypoint), "stuck" (local pathfinding failed, retrying periodically), "waiting_for_chunk" (next waypoint's chunk isn't loaded, waiting per the catch-up strategy), "arrived", or "failed_no_path" (the chunk-gate route couldn't be computed — see the console for why). Read-only.

title: [Long Navigation] Viewers
description: Gets, adds, removes, or replaces the list of players who can see the (virtual) entity of a long navigation. Only relevant for long navigations created from a numeric ID rather than a real entity.

title: Block Display
description: A fake display entity that renders a block. Supports all common display properties (scale, translation, rotations, glow, brightness, shadow, view range, billboard) plus a block data string that defines which block is shown. Fully serializable for persistent storage in Skript variables.
type_usage: Created via 'set %objects% to a new fake block display'.

title: Chunk Path Record
description: Represents the chunk-to-chunk pathfinding record of an analyzed chunk: the world it belongs to and the gates (connections to neighboring chunks) computed for it. Obtained via 'chunk path [record] of %chunk%', which returns nothing if the chunk was never registered.
type_usage: Obtained via 'chunk path [record] of %chunk%'.

title: Path Cost Rule
description: A single pathfinding cost rule: a set of blocks and/or block tags that, when matched, apply a given movement cost instead of the world's default cost. Used to build a custom rule set passed to 'register chunk path of %chunk%'.
type_usage: Created via 'a new path cost rule [with cost %number%]', then populated via the blocks/tags list expressions.

title: [Long Navigation] Type
description: A long-distance, cost-rule aware pathfinding session — the long-distance counterpart to the 'navigation' type. Computes a coarse chunk-gate route between a start and an end location (using registered chunk path records and the world's path cost rules), then walks the real terrain toward that route waypoint by waypoint, recalculating short segments as needed instead of precomputing the whole distant path at once. Like a normal navigation, it can be created from a numeric ID (virtual entity, requires PacketEvents to send movement packets to viewers) or a real entity (moved via teleport).
type_usage: Created via 'a new long fake navigation with id %number% ...' or 'a new long navigation with entity %entity% ...'.

title: Replace with Regex (Section)
description:
Runs the section once for each occurrence of the regex(es) in each of the given texts.
Inside the section, 'matched text' contains the text matched by the regex and 'replaced text' (defaults to the matched text) can be changed: at the end of each iteration, the matched zone is replaced by it.
'matched group %integer%' and 'matched group named %string%' give access to the regex capture groups.
When several regexes are given, they are applied one after the other on the result of the previous one.
Behaves like a loop: 'continue' goes to the next occurrence and 'exit loop' stops the section (the replacements already made are kept).

title: Song
description: Song data that holds all the original notes and the original modifiers.
type_usage: new pxmusic song from import "first_defence.json"

title: Clear Session
description:
Clears the menu session of the given player(s).
This will remove the content of the gui they have open, but will not close the gui itself.
If 'refresh' is specified, the player's gui will be refreshed to reflect the cleared session.
A menu, session or window keyword is required; bare 'clear' keeps Skript's variable deletion behavior.
syntax_pattern:
clear [the] (menu [(session|window)]|session|window) %menusession% [and refresh]
clear [the] menu (session|window) of %player% [and refresh]

title: Refresh Menu Session
description:
Refresh the menu session, updating the inventory view.
If a slot number is provided, only that slot will be refreshed.
If no slot number is provided, the entire inventory will be refreshed.
Does nothing if the menu receptacle mode is static or the session is not active.
syntax_pattern:
refresh [the slot %number% in] [the] (menu [(session|window)]|session|window) %menusession%
refresh [the slot %number% in] [the] menu (session|window) of %player%

title: Game Effects with Data
description:
Creates game effects that require some extra information, such as colors, particle counts, or block data.
Game effects consist of combinations particles and/or sounds that are used in Minecraft, such as the bone meal particles, the sound of footsteps on a specific block, or the particles and sound of breaking a splash potion.
Game effects not present here do not require data and can be found in the Game Effect type.
Data requirements vary from version to version, so these docs are only accurate for the most recent Minecraft version at time of release.
syntax_pattern:
[record] song (of|using) %itemtype%
[dispenser] black smoke effect [(in|with|using) [the] direction] %direction%
[dispenser] white smoke effect [(in|with|using) [the] direction] %direction%
%itemtype/blockdata% [foot]step[s] sound [effect]
%itemtype/blockdata% (break|destroy) effect
%itemtype/blockdata% (break|destroy) effect with sound
destroy progress effect on the %direction% [side|face]
destroy progress effect on the %direction% [side|face] with sound
%color% [splash] potion break effect
%color% instant [splash] potion break effect
compost[er] [fill[ing]] (succe(ss|ed)|fail[ure|ed]) sound [effect]
villager plant grow[th] effect [(with|using) %number% particles]
[fake] bone meal effect [(with|using) %number% particles]
(electric|lightning[ rod]|copper) spark effect [(in|using|along) the (x|y|z) axis]
sculk (charge|spread) effect [(with|using) data %integer%]
ender dragon egg teleport[ing] [to %vector%] effect
shulker teleport[ing] [to %vector%] effect
consumable teleport[ing] [to %vector%] effect
enderman teleport[ing] [to %vector%] effect
[finish] brush[ing] %itemtype/blockdata% effect
trial spawner detect[ing|s] [%number%] player[s] effect
ominous trial spawner detect[ing|s] [%number%] player[s] effect
[ominous] trial spawner spawn[ing] [mob] effect
[ominous] trial spawner spawn[ing] [mob] effect with sound
bee growth effect [(with|using) %number% particles]
[ominous] [trial] vault activate effect
[ominous] [trial] vault deactivate effect
trial spawner become[ing] [not] ominous effect
[ominous] trial spawner spawn[ing] item effect
place turtle egg effect [(with|using) %number% particles]
[mace] smash attack effect [(with|using) %number% particles]

title: Midpoint
description: Get the midpoint between two vectors or two locations in the same world.

title: Biome
description:
All possible biomes Minecraft uses to generate a world.
NOTE: Minecraft namespaces are supported, ex: 'minecraft:basalt_deltas'.
type_usage: badlands, badlands forest, bamboo jungle, basalt deltas, beach, birch forest, black forest, cherry grove, cold beach, cold ocean, cold taiga, crimson forest, dappled forest, dark forest, deep cold ocean, deep dark, deep frozen ocean, deep lukewarm ocean, deep ocean, desert, dripstone caves, end barrens, end highlands, end midlands, eroded badlands, eroded mesa, flower forest, forest, frozen ocean, frozen peaks, frozen river, giant spruce taiga, giant tree taiga, gravelly mountains, grove, hell, ice plains spikes, ice plains with spikes, ice spikes, jagged peaks, jungle, jungle edge, lukewarm ocean, lush caves, mangrove swamp, marsh, meadow, mesa, mesa forest, mountains, mushroom fields, mushroom island, nether, nether wastes, ocean, old growth birch forest, old growth pine taiga, old growth spruce taiga, pale garden, plains, river, roofed forest, savanna, savanna plateau, sea, shattered savanna, sky, small end islands, snowy beach, snowy plains, snowy slopes, snowy taiga, snowy tundra, soul sand valley, sparse jungle, spiked ice plains, stone shore, stony peaks, stony shore, sulfur caves, sunflower plains, swamp, swampland, taiga, tall birch forest, the end, the void, void, warm ocean, warped forest, windswept forest, windswept gravelly hills, windswept hills, windswept savanna, wooded badlands, wooded mesa, wooded mountains

title: Song from Import
description:
Imports a song from plugins/PxMusic/imported
It will automatically register the imported song as well.

title: On Netty Packet
description: Listens to any incoming or outgoing packet on the packet's processing thread. Equivalent to 'on any packet netty processed'. Packets can be changed or cancelled except at monitor priority. Bukkit operations requiring the server thread must not be used here.

title: General - On Packet
description: Listen to incoming/outgoing packets, more on [the wiki](https://github.com/3add/PacketEventsSK/wiki/Events)

title: General - Packet Type Bound
description: See in which direction a packet (or packettype) is bound

title: General - Cancel Packet
description:
Used to cancel the packet in a packet receive/send event.
This just means that the packet won't be processed/sent.

title: Kill Packet Entity
description: Kills the packet entity

title: Packet Team Members
description: Adds or removes players, entities, packet entities or entry strings from a packet team. Players use their names; other entities use UUIDs. Adding moves the entry from its previous team definition. Removal only affects the specified team. Send the team packet to apply changes to viewers. The fake and packet prefixes are aliases.
syntax_pattern:
add %entities/packetentities/texts% to [the] (fake|packet) team %packet%
remove %entities/packetentities/texts% from [the] (fake|packet) team %packet%

title: Fake Entity - Spawn Fake Entity
description: Spawn a packet entity at a location. An existing managed entity is moved. To move use teleport.

title: Fake Entity - Ride
description:
Make fake entities ride another entity (fake or real), or remove them as passengers.
**Note: Real entities are just a single packet being sent, when a player relogs, changes worlds or some other circumstances the passengers will be altered by the vanilla server.**

title: Teleport Packet Entities
description: Moves packet entities and updates the position and world used when restoring their viewers.

title: General - Fetch Skin
description:
Used to fetch a player skin.
**This is processed on an async thread and thus will pause your code until it's been loaded.**
syntax_pattern:
fetch skin (from|of) player (named|with name) %text% and store (it|the result) in %~objects%
set %~objects% to [fetch] skin (from|of) player (named|with name) %text%

title: General - Send/Receive Packet
description: Used to force the server to send or receive a packet, optionally silently. (silent means it won't trigger on packet send or receive)

title: Packet Entity Viewers
description: Adds online viewers or permanently removes viewers, including offline players. Updates persistence tracking. Removing the last viewer hides the entity without destroying it.
syntax_pattern:
add %players% to [the] viewers of (fake|packet) entit(y|ies) %packetentities%
remove %offline players% from [the] viewers of (fake|packet) entit(y|ies) %packetentities%

title: Simple Skin - Player Displayed Skin
description:
Set the displayed skin of a player for a set of viewers.
Internally everything is handled by the addon (fully packet based).
Add 'with persistent' to override subsequent player profile packets, including
tracking refreshes. Without it, the skin is applied once and later profile
updates may replace it. No repeating task is used. Overrides end when the
target disconnects or the addon disables; viewer-specific overrides also
end when that viewer disconnects. A global change replaces all existing
viewer overrides. A viewer-specific change replaces that viewer's override.
syntax_pattern: set displayed skin of %players% to %skin% [for %players%] [with persistent]

title: Fake Inventory Slots
description: Displays fake items in raw slots of the current inventory view. Add 'with persistent' to keep overriding server updates and refresh after clicks. Without it, the display is one-time and replaces any existing persistent override for that slot. Player inventory: 0 crafting result, 1-4 crafting inputs, 5-8 armor, 9-35 storage, 36-44 hotbar, 45 offhand. Container slots use their own numbering; wait one tick after opening. Player-inventory overrides last until disconnect; container overrides end on close. Items are visual only. Creative mode can request real item creation. Reset slots to restore their current real items and remove persistence. Reset/clear the whole fake inventory to remove all overrides.
syntax_pattern:
make fake inventory slot[s] %numbers% (as|to) %item type% to %players% [with persistent]
reset fake inventory slot[s] %numbers% for %players%
(reset|clear) [all] fake inventory [slots] for %players%

title: Fake Blocks
description: Shows client-side block data without changing the world. Persistence defaults to false. Persistent blocks block outgoing updates to their positions and are reapplied after chunk updates and reconnects until reset or cleared; they are not saved across server restarts. Reset restores current real block data. Clear removes every managed fake block for the players. These blocks have no server-side collision or drops. Use block data such as gold block.
syntax_pattern:
make fake blocks at %locations% as %block data% to %players% [with persistent]
reset fake blocks at %locations% for %players%
clear [all] fake blocks for %players%

title: Simple Glow - Entity Glow State
description:
Set the glow state of an entity for a set of viewers.
Internally everything is handled by the addon. (fully packet based)

title: Fake Equipment
description: Changes the equipment shown on real living entities for chosen viewers without changing inventories. Accepts player's held item or player's helmet. Uses Skript equipment slots, such as main hand and helmet slot. Add 'with persistent' to keep the appearance across equipment updates, tracking changes and reconnects. Each viewer/target/slot stores only one item. Overrides end when a non-player target unloads or dies, or the plugin stops. Without the flag this is a one-time update and replaces the previous persistent override for that slot. Reset restores current real equipment and removes the persistent overrides. Does not change the owner's inventory or first-person held item.
syntax_pattern:
make fake equipment %equipment slot% of %entities% as %item type% to %players% [with persistent]
reset fake equipment %equipment slots% of %entities% for %players%
(reset|clear) [all] fake equipment of %entities% for %players%

title: Fake Entity - All Fake Entities
description: Used to get a list of all fake entities that are viewable by least a single player

title: New Packet Team
description: Creates a team packet. Name is required. Sending creates or updates the team automatically for each viewer.

title: Packet Entity - Sprinting State
description: The packet entity sprinting state property. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: Fake Entity - Player Username
description: The fake player profile name, supplied at construction. Read-only. Value type: String. Applies to player and supported subclasses. Read-only.

title: Packet Team Of Entity
description: Gets the packet team assigned to entity IDs, fake entities or Bukkit entities. Use 'add player to packet team {_team}' to assign a team. Delete/reset clears the assignment; send the old team again to remove the client entry. Unknown IDs are rejected.

title: Fake Entity - From Entity UUID
description: Retrieve a fake entity from it's entity uuid, this only works for spawned fake entities

title: Entity Meta - Health
description: The living entity health metadata value. Value type: Number. Applies to livingentity and supported subclasses. Supports set. When editing metadata copied from a packet, set packet meta back to the edited object.

title: Entity Meta - Display Transform Interpolation Duration
description: The display transform interpolation duration property. Value type: Timespan. Applies to display and supported subclasses. Supports set. When editing metadata copied from a packet, set packet meta back to the edited object.
syntax_pattern:
[the] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] display transform interpolation duration of %entitymeta%
%entitymeta%'[s] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] display transform interpolation duration

title: Packet Entity - Display See Through State
description: The packet entity display see through state property. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.
syntax_pattern: meta [field] display see through [state] of (fake|packet) entity %packetentities%

title: Fake Entity - Entity Viewers
description: Changing this list adds/removes viewers of the fake entity. Value type: Player[]. Applies to entity and supported subclasses. Supports set.

title: General - New Packet
description:
Create a new packet from a packet type.
### Available Packets and their fields
* **block break animation** fields:
  - `entity id`
  - `block position (position, pos)`
  - `destroy stage (breaking stage, stage)`
* **entity metadata** fields:
  - `entity id (id)`
  - `entity metadata (entity meta, metadata, meta)`
* **camera** fields:
  - `entity id (camera id, id)`
* **select bundle item** fields:
  - `slot id (id)`
  - `selected item index (selected index, item index, index)`
* **update sign** fields:
  - `location vector (location)`
  - `sign lines (lines)`
  - `sign side (side)`
* **teams** fields:
  - `name (team name)`
  - `entries`
  - `display name`
  - `prefix`
  - `suffix`
  - `color`
  - `name tag visibility`
  - `collision rule`
  - `friendly fire`
  - `see invisible teammates`
* **effect** fields:
  - `effect id`
  - `position`
  - `data`
  - `global event`
* **block change** fields:
  - `block position (block pos, position, pos)`
  - `block state (state, block data, data)`
* **entity status** fields:
  - `entity id (id)`
  - `status`
* **block entity data** fields:
  - `block position (block pos, position, pos)`
  - `block entity type (entity type, type)`
  - `nbt compound (nbt, compound)`
* **block action** fields:
  - `block position (position, pos)`
  - `action id`
  - `action data`
  - `block type id`
* **hurt animation** fields:
  - `entity id`
  - `yaw`
* **game test highlight pos** fields:
  - `absolute position (absolute pos, abs position, abs pos, position, pos)`
  - `relative position (relative pos, rel position, rel pos)`
* **interact entity** fields:
  - `entity id (id)`
  - `interaction hand (hand)`
  - `location vector (location, loc)`
  - `sneaking state (sneaking)`
* **entity velocity** fields:
  - `entity id (id)`
  - `velocity vector (vector, velocity)`
* **destroy entities** fields:
  - `entity ids (ids)`
* **open sign editor** fields:
  - `block position (block pos, position, pos)`
  - `sign side (side)`

title: Team Name
description: The scoreboard identifier of the team. Changing it recreates the team for viewers when sent. Send the team packet to apply changes to viewers.

title: Packet Entity - Display Block Data
description: The packet entity display block data property. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: General - Packet Type
description: The packet type of a packet

title: Packet Entity - Display Right Rotation
description: The quaternion applied after the display scale. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: Packet Entity - Display Billboard Constraints
description: The packet entity display billboard constraints property. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: Packet Entity - Invisible State
description: The packet entity invisible state property. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: Entity Meta - Display Item
description: The display item property. Value type: ItemType. Applies to item display and supported subclasses. Supports set. When editing metadata copied from a packet, set packet meta back to the edited object.
syntax_pattern:
[the] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] display item [stack] of %entitymeta%
%entitymeta%'[s] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] display item [stack]

title: Packet Entity - Display Item
description: The packet entity display item property. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: Entity Meta - Entity ID
description: The numeric network entity ID. Read-only. Value type: Number. Applies to entity and supported subclasses. Read-only. When editing metadata copied from a packet, set packet meta back to the edited object.

title: Packet Entity - Gravity State
description: True enables gravity; false disables it. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: Team Entries
description: The player names or entity UUID strings assigned to the team. Supports set, add, remove and reset. Send the team packet to apply changes to viewers.

title: Packet Entity - Elytra Flying State

title: Packet Entity - Display Translation

title: Fake Entity - Entity Meta Data
description: Returns live metadata for fake entities, or a metadata snapshot for real entities. Changing a snapshot does not change the server entity: send it in an entity metadata packet to chosen viewers. For persistent player glow, use 'set packet glow state of player to true for player'.

title: Packet Entity - Display Text
description: The text component shown by a text display. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: Entity Meta - Elytra Flying State
description: The elytra flying state property. Value type: Boolean. Applies to entity and supported subclasses. Supports set. When editing metadata copied from a packet, set packet meta back to the edited object.

[the] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] elytra flying [state] of %entitymeta%
%entitymeta%'[s] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] elytra flying [state]

syntax_pattern:
[the] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] display teleport interpolation duration of %entitymeta%
%entitymeta%'[s] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] display teleport interpolation duration

description: The display transformation scale vector. Value type: Vector. Applies to display and supported subclasses. Supports set. When editing metadata copied from a packet, set packet meta back to the edited object.

[the] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] display scale of %entitymeta%
%entitymeta%'[s] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] display scale

title: Packet Entity - Silent State
description: The packet entity silent state property. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: Packet Entity - Interaction Width
description: The packet entity interaction width property. Supports set, delete and reset; unsupported entity types are rejected.

title: Entity Meta - Display Text Shadowed State
description: The display text shadowed state property. Value type: Boolean. Applies to text display and supported subclasses. Supports set. When editing metadata copied from a packet, set packet meta back to the edited object.
syntax_pattern:
[the] [(fake|packet)] [entity] meta [field] display (shadowed [state]|text shadowed state) of %entitymeta%

title: General - Packet Field
description:
Gets or sets a field's value from a packet by its name.

### Available Packets and their fields
* **block break animation** fields:
  - `entity id`
  - `block position (position, pos)`
  - `destroy stage (breaking stage, stage)`
* **entity metadata** fields:
  - `entity id (id)`
  - `entity metadata (entity meta, metadata, meta)`
* **camera** fields:
  - `entity id (camera id, id)`
* **select bundle item** fields:
  - `slot id (id)`
  - `selected item index (selected index, item index, index)`
* **update sign** fields:
  - `location vector (location)`
  - `sign lines (lines)`
  - `sign side (side)`
* **teams** fields:
  - `name (team name)`
  - `entries`
  - `display name`
  - `prefix`
  - `suffix`
  - `color`
  - `name tag visibility`
  - `collision rule`
  - `friendly fire`
  - `see invisible teammates`
* **effect** fields:
  - `effect id`
  - `position`
  - `data`
  - `global event`
* **block change** fields:
  - `block position (block pos, position, pos)`
  - `block state (state, block data, data)`
* **entity status** fields:
  - `entity id (id)`
  - `status`
* **block entity data** fields:
  - `block position (block pos, position, pos)`
  - `block entity type (entity type, type)`
  - `nbt compound (nbt, compound)`
* **block action** fields:
  - `block position (position, pos)`
  - `action id`
  - `action data`
  - `block type id`
* **hurt animation** fields:
  - `entity id`
  - `yaw`
* **game test highlight pos** fields:
  - `absolute position (absolute pos, abs position, abs pos, position, pos)`
  - `relative position (relative pos, rel position, rel pos)`
* **interact entity** fields:
  - `entity id (id)`
  - `interaction hand (hand)`
  - `location vector (location, loc)`
  - `sneaking state (sneaking)`
* **entity velocity** fields:
  - `entity id (id)`
  - `velocity vector (vector, velocity)`
* **destroy entities** fields:
  - `entity ids (ids)`
* **open sign editor** fields:
  - `block position (block pos, position, pos)`
  - `sign side (side)`
